jobs.excerpt: Talent Acquisition Sourcer Location: Remote (Canada-wide) Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent Category: Corporate & Support Team / Talent Acquisition About VetCare VetCare is a proud Canadian community of veterinary practices committed to offering exceptional patient care and client experiences.
jobs.description:
Talent Acquisition Sourcer

Location: Remote (Canada-wide)

Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

Category: Corporate & Support Team / Talent Acquisition

About VetCare

VetCare is a proud Canadian community of veterinary practices committed to offering exceptional patient care and client experiences. We combine the personal touch, local culture, and clinical autonomy of independent practices with the robust support, resources, and connection of a nationwide network.

At VetCare, our values guide everything we do:

  • Come together as one: We support each other as one team.

  • Always focus on the patient: We prioritize clinical excellence, patient care, and client connection.

  • Raise the bar: We pursue continuous improvement, personal development, and positive change.

  • Engage with empathy: We seek understanding and lead with compassion in every interaction.

Position Purpose

The Talent Acquisition Sourcer / Junior Recruiter is the core outbound pipeline engine for VetCare’s national talent team. This role is built specifically for a true hunter—someone energized by proactive search, direct headhunting, and tracking down passive clinical professionals across Canada, with an acute focus on rural, northern, and hard-to-fill markets.

We already have great recruiters managing relationship stewardship and process management; what we need now is an outbound specialist who thrives on uncovering hidden talent and feeding qualified Doctors of Veterinary Medicine (DVMs) and Registered Veterinary Technologists/Technicians (RVTs) to our senior recruiters. You will partner closely with our internal recruiting team as your primary stakeholders, handling screening and interview handoffs while providing the administrative velocity that keeps pipelines moving. Direct exposure to multi-site practice managers and regional leadership will serve as a natural operational growth path as your role evolves.

What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)

Passive Sourcing & Pipeline Hunting (50%)

  • Execute aggressive outbound headhunting strategies across specialized platforms, including LinkedIn Recruiter, provincial veterinary licensing registries, university faculties, associations (CVMA), and clinical networks.

  • Target, map, and nurture talent communities in persistent, hard-to-fill markets (e.g., Northern Ontario, rural Alberta, interior British Columbia, and rural Atlantic Canada).

  • Craft highly customized, compelling cold-outreach messaging that cuts through the noise, articulating VetCare’s clinical autonomy, practice culture, and sustainable workload model.

  • Conduct initial phone screens to evaluate clinical interests, licensing eligibility, relocation appetite, and mutual culture fit before handing warm leads off to our senior recruiters.

Recruitment Coordination & Team Support (30%)

  • Partner side-by-side with our senior recruiters to manage candidate logistics, schedule seamless recruiter interview handoffs, and ensure candidate momentum across multiple Canadian time zones.

  • Maintain rigorous ATS hygiene—tracking lead statuses, pipeline movement, and sourcing channel metrics to keep team dashboards accurate and actionable.

  • Support pre-employment administration, including professional clinical reference checks, regulatory credential verifications with provincial colleges, and offer package documentation.

  • Maintain job board postings across regional and academic platforms, ensuring alignment with provincial standards and pay transparency legislation.

Market Intelligence & Candidate Engagement (20%)

  • Serve as an engaging, authentic first contact for clinicians, navigating sensitive discussions around burnout, relocation barriers, and scheduling needs with high empathy.

  • Keep a pulse on competitor offerings, compensation trends, and provincial licensing shifts, sharing real-time market insights with the talent acquisition team.

  • Support early-career student outreach, campus career events, and RVT externship pipelines alongside the senior recruiters.

What You Bring (Qualifications & Competencies)

  • Hunter Mindset (Essential): You are a relentless outbound sourcer who enjoys the thrill of the chase. You prefer prospecting, direct outreach, and cold pipeline creation over administrative "farming" or waiting for applications to arrive.

  • Experience: 1–3 years of hands-on recruitment sourcing or coordination experience within an agency or in-house talent team. Prior experience in healthcare, locum staffing, or niche/scarce-talent industries is a strong asset.

  • Education: Post-secondary diploma or degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Communications, or a related field (or equivalent practical work experience).

  • Sourcing & Digital Tools: Strong working command of Boolean logic, LinkedIn Recruiter workflows, and modern ATS/CRM systems. Proficient with Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace.

  • Canadian Regulatory Landscape: Foundational understanding of Canadian employment standards; exposure to provincial veterinary colleges (e.g., CVO, ABVMA, BCVMA) is considered an asset.

  • Bilingualism: Fluency in French is considered an asset.

  • Resilience & EQ: High emotional intelligence to build instant rapport with guarded medical professionals, combined with the persistence needed to thrive in tight candidate pools.

Key Success Measures (KPIs)

  • Outbound Pipeline Delivery: Volume of vetted, qualified DVM and RVT candidates passed along to internal recruiters monthly.

  • Sourcing Velocity: Conversion rates from initial cold outreach to completed preliminary screen.

  • Hard-to-Hire Impact: Consistent candidate discovery and engagement in remote, rural, and high-vacancy clinical regions.

  • Coordination Efficiency: Smooth handoffs to internal recruiters with minimal turnaround delay or candidate drop-off.

  • ATS Integrity: Pristine candidate records, updated stage tracking, and clear communication notes.

What We Offer (Compensation & Benefits)

  • Competitive Compensation: Base salary range of $65,000 – $75,000 CAD per year, commensurate with sourcing depth and industry background.

  • Incentive Potential: Eligible for an annual performance bonus (5%–10%) plus placement-based milestone bonuses per DVM hire retained past 6 months.

  • Work Arrangement: 100% remote work flexibility from anywhere in Canada.

  • Comprehensive Benefits: Group coverage including extended health, dental, vision care, life insurance, and disability.

  • Professional Growth: Clear advancement path into full-cycle recruiting and regional operations, supported by an annual professional development budget for recruitment training, certifications, and HR memberships.

  • Collaborative Culture: A supportive internal team where your sourcing impact directly shapes clinic success and community pet care.

VetCare is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion across all our practices and corporate teams. If you require accommodations at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization.We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire customer journey.
  • We're taking autonomous search mainstream, making product discovery more intuitive and conversational for customers, and more profitable for businesses.
  • We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey.
  • We're designing the future of autonomous marketing, taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do.
And we're building all of that on the intelligence of a single AI engine — Loomi — so that personalization isn't only autonomous…it's also consistent.From retail to financial services, hospitality to gaming, businesses use Bloomreach to drive higher growth and lasting loyalty. We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora.

Bloomreach is building the future of commerce experiences, helping businesses create more relevant, intelligent, and measurable interactions with their customers. As AI reshapes how people discover, evaluate, and buy products, we are expanding our capabilities in Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) -helping brands become visible, credible, and preferred in the new generation of AI-driven search and answer experiences.

We are looking for a commercial leader to help turn a high-quality AEO product into a scaled, repeatable growth business inside Bloomreach.

The opportunity

The AEO product has strong product and engineering leadership along with proof points selling to large enterprises and SMBs. The next phase is to accelerate the business into the next phase of growth with B2C brands.

This is a build-and-scale role - not a traditional sales leadership position focused only on optimizing an established motion. You will own the commercial strategy, validate where the product wins, shape the sales and customer lifecycle around those insights, and create the operating model needed for sustainable growth.

You will lead the existing four-person AEO commercial team, while also building a strong partnership with Bloomreach’s broader sales organization. A central part of the role will be determining how AEO can be cross-sold into Bloomreach’s existing customer base or co-sold with existing Bloomreach products - and how our core sellers can confidently identify, position, and help sell the product as part of broader customer solutions.

What you will own

1. Establish product–market fit in B2C Enterprise Brands segment

  • Translate product strengths into a crisp commercial narrative that resonates with B2C Enterprise Brands.
  • Build a disciplined learning loop across prospects, customers, partners/broader ecosystem, Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Customer Success.
  • Personal product mastery: Identify where the current product is strongest, where it needs to evolve, and which opportunities should be prioritized commercially.
  • Turn early wins and customer evidence into repeatable messaging, qualification criteria, sales plays, and proof points.
  • Help champions turn an emerging AEO mandate into a funded initiative: shape the business case with marketing leadership, secure executive sponsorship, and align relevant teams and budgets.

2. Scale to $10M ARR

  • Create and execute the commercial plan to grow the business to $10M ARR.
  • Establish the right balance of new-logo acquisition, expansion, renewal, and strategic account development.
  • Build a measurable operating cadence across pipeline creation, conversion, deal velocity, forecast accuracy, retention, expansion, and team productivity.
  • Set the right coverage model, territories, quotas, incentives, capacity plan, and hiring roadmap as the business scales.
  • Personally engage in strategic opportunities and executive-level customer relationships where they can materially accelerate growth.

3. Build a high-performing AEO commercial team

  • Lead, coach, and develop the current AEs and CSMs, creating clarity on roles, expectations, priorities, and measures of success.
  • Strengthen the end-to-end customer journey from qualification through implementation, adoption, renewal, and expansion.
  • Define the skills, profiles, and structure needed for the next stage of growth.
  • Hire selectively as evidence supports expansion of the team.
  • Create a culture of accountability, customer empathy, experimentation, and continuous improvement.

4. Create the cross-sell and partner motion with the core sales organization

  • Develop a clear strategy for introducing AEO into Bloomreach’s existing customer base and co-selling alongside existing Bloomreach sellers.
  • Identify the customer segments, account signals, trigger events, and use cases that indicate cross-sell potential.
  • Design a practical engagement model between the AEO team and Bloomreach’s main sales organization—including ownership, qualification, account planning, compensation, handoffs, and deal support.
  • Equip core sellers with the messaging, training, discovery questions, collateral, demos, and commercial plays needed to identify and open AEO opportunities.
  • Build trust and shared incentives so the AEO team is viewed as a growth partner—not a competing sales channel.
  • Establish a repeatable model for specialist-led, core-sales-assisted, and core-sales-led opportunities.

5. Partner cross-functionally to shape the business

  • Work closely with Product and Engineering to connect market feedback to roadmap priorities and commercial readiness.
  • Partner with Marketing on positioning, category creation, demand generation, customer proof, events, and thought leadership.
  • Collaborate with Finance and Revenue Operations on planning, forecasting, reporting, compensation, and business performance.
  • Bring customer and market insight to the broader Bloomreach leadership team and help shape the role of AEO in the company’s overall strategy.
  • AI operating skills. Use AI tooling like Codex and Claude Code to test hypotheses against company data, inspect deals, build forecasts, and build leverage into GTM

What success looks like

In the first 90 days

  • Establish Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) Repeatability - demonstrating that the team can win cleanly within a tightly defined target sandbox, rather than taking any random deal that comes along including
  • ICP Concentration:80%+ of closed-won deals match your designated Ideal Customer Profile firmographics and personas.

  • Work closely with data analysts, data engineers, and machine learning engineers to understand their needs - and evolve the Doximity data stack to meet them.
  • Build the foundations that make client-facing data delivery safe and repeatable - per-client data isolation, access controls, and auditability.
  • Build and operate the MCP-based tooling and agentic workflows through which analysts and clients interact with the data platform - and the data it manifests - by conversation rather than tickets.
  • Work in a HIPAA-regulated environment where the right people and systems reach the data they need and nothing more - masking policies, scoped roles, audit trails, and approval gates that hold up to scrutiny from auditors and clients alike.
  • Understand what our data product teams are trying to achieve, and design solutions that maximize the time they spend on their goals and minimize the time lost to technical hurdles.
  • Help strengthen our software engineering culture within the data organization, leading by example.
  • Diagnose development, performance, and stability issues in our core data pipelines and Python libraries, and help product data teams resolve problems that need platform-level expertise.

What we’re looking for

  • We’re seeking a strong Python engineer who brings deep professional experience in data engineering and internal tooling, with a track record of supporting multiple product teams simultaneously.
  • Especially valuable experience:
    • Snowflake beyond querying - governance features, cloning, Time Travel and Fail-safe, hybrid tables, streams, and data lifecycle capabilities, Cortex suite of AI tools, Snowpark Container Services, or data sharing.
    • Kafka, change data capture (CDC) like Debezium, and database internals - a significant portion of our pipeline work lives here.
    • Operating under HIPAA, SOC 2, or similar - least-privilege design, masking and de-identification, audit logging.
    • Building or operating agentic and MCP-based tooling.
    • Apache Airflow and AWS.
    • Container-based development workflows (Kubernetes, Docker) - useful, but secondary to the above.
    • We don’t expect all of these. Depth in Python, SQL, and data engineering is the requirement; the rest tells us where you’ll ramp fastest.
  • The ideal candidate will demonstrate expert fluency in Python and an understanding of programming language internals.
  • Advanced knowledge of software engineering practices and testing methodologies is a must; you are foremost an engineer, making you passionate about high-quality code, automated testing, and software engineering best practices. You demonstrate this both within your own team and with colleagues beyond it.
  • You have deep fluency in SQL, using analytical databases, and are able to practically employ and orchestrate user defined functions, stored procedures, and other database-oriented solutions to deliver performant and cost-effective database-driven solutions.
  • You have worked with data that carries real handling obligations - PHI, PII, or client-confidential data - under a framework like HIPAA, SOC 2, or GDPR. You design for least-privilege access by default, you think in terms of blast radius and auditability, and you treat these as engineering problems rather than paperwork.
  • Your ability and drive to self-manage, prioritize tasks, and deliver functional solutions will be crucial to succeeding in this role.
  • You treat AI-driven engineering as part of the craft, not a novelty - agentic coding tools, MCP-based tooling, and automation that removes toil - and you invest in keeping your practice current as the tools evolve. You communicate clearly in writing and in person, and you keep your work legible through practices like clear change management and well-documented code. You see your teammates as your first customer.

  • We have over 500 private repositories in Github containing our pipelines, our own internal multi-functional tools, and open-source projects

  • Our company core values
  • Our recruiting process
  • Our product development cycle
  • Our on-boarding & mentorship process

Compensation

  • Equity (where applicable)

Specific compensation details will be discussed during the interview process.

  • Flexible paid time off and company holidays

Why You'll Love Working Here

At Doximity, you'll join a mission-driven company where your work has a meaningful impact on healthcare. We believe great ideas come from empowered teams, and we're committed to creating an environment where people can do their best work.

  • Make a real impact. Help build products that support over a million healthcare professionals and ultimately improve patient care.

Enterprise Transformation Director – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Enterprise Transformation Director is responsible for defining, leading, and overseeing the organization's enterprise-wide transformation strategy to improve business performance, operational efficiency, financial sustainability, customer experience, and long-term competitiveness.

Within the Insurance & Investments sector, the role drives large-scale transformation initiatives across business operations, technology, organizational structures, digital capabilities, governance, and customer-facing services.

The incumbent translates corporate strategy into an integrated transformation roadmap, oversees strategic programmes and transformation portfolios, and ensures initiatives deliver measurable business value. The role works closely with the CEO, executive leadership, business unit heads, and external partners to drive sustainable organizational change and achieve strategic objectives.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Enterprise Transformation Strategy & Leadership

  • Define and lead the organization's enterprise-wide transformation strategy, vision, and execution roadmap.
  • Translate corporate strategy into transformation priorities, strategic initiatives, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Identify opportunities for business model innovation, organizational improvement, operational modernization, and sustainable growth.
  • Align transformation initiatives with corporate objectives, market developments, customer expectations, and regulatory requirements.
  • Advise the CEO and executive leadership on transformation priorities, investment decisions, and strategic opportunities.

B. Business Model & Operating Model Transformation

  • Lead enterprise-wide operating model redesign and organizational transformation initiatives.
  • Evaluate existing business structures, processes, capabilities, and operating models to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Drive business process reengineering, simplification, standardization, and automation.
  • Oversee transformation of insurance operations, investment services, distribution channels, and customer service functions.
  • Improve organizational agility, productivity, cost efficiency, and service delivery.

C. Digital & Technology Transformation

  • Oversee enterprise-wide digital transformation and technology modernization initiatives.
  • Drive adoption of cloud platforms, artificial intelligence, automation, advanced analytics, and digital business solutions.
  • Lead modernization and integration of enterprise applications, core insurance systems, investment platforms, and customer management technologies.
  • Collaborate with technology leadership to ensure digital investments support business strategy.
  • Promote innovation, data-driven decision-making, and technology-enabled business growth.

D. Transformation Portfolio & Programme Governance

  • Oversee the organization's strategic transformation portfolio, programmes, and major initiatives.
  • Establish enterprise transformation governance frameworks, performance controls, and reporting mechanisms.
  • Monitor transformation milestones, budgets, resource requirements, risks, and dependencies.
  • Coordinate transformation directors, programme managers, project leaders, and cross-functional teams.
  • Ensure initiatives are delivered within approved timelines, budgets, and quality standards.

E. Financial Performance & Value Creation

  • Develop transformation business cases, investment proposals, and financial impact assessments.
  • Identify opportunities to improve profitability, reduce operating costs, and optimize capital and resource utilization.
  • Monitor transformation expenditure, financial performance, and expected return on investment.
  • Establish benefits realization frameworks to track financial and non-financial outcomes.
  • Ensure transformation investments generate measurable and sustainable business value.

F. Organizational Change & Cultural Transformation

  • Lead enterprise-wide change management and organizational development strategies.
  • Work with HR and business leaders to drive workforce transformation, leadership alignment, and cultural change.
  • Build organizational readiness and employee engagement for major transformation initiatives.
  • Oversee communication, training, capability development, and change adoption programmes.
  • Promote a culture of innovation, accountability, adaptability, and continuous improvement.

G. Risk, Compliance & Regulatory Transformation

  • Ensure enterprise transformation initiatives align with applicable insurance, investment, financial services, and regulatory requirements.
  • Oversee transformation-related strategic, operational, financial, technology, and compliance risks.
  • Collaborate with risk, compliance, legal, and internal audit teams to strengthen governance and controls.
  • Drive initiatives that improve operational resilience, data governance, cybersecurity, and regulatory readiness.
  • Ensure transformation programmes maintain appropriate oversight, accountability, and auditability.

H. Executive Stakeholder & Board Engagement

  • Build strong relationships with the CEO, board members, executive committees, and business unit leaders.
  • Present transformation strategies, performance reports, financial outcomes, and strategic recommendations.
  • Lead enterprise transformation steering committees and executive review meetings.
  • Manage relationships with external consultants, strategic partners, technology providers, and regulators.
  • Ensure executive alignment and accountability for transformation outcomes.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree or MBA is strongly preferred.
  • 15+ years of progressive experience in enterprise transformation, corporate strategy, business transformation, management consulting, or executive programme leadership.
  • At least 5–7 years in a senior director-level or enterprise transformation leadership position.
  • Proven experience leading large-scale, enterprise-wide transformation initiatives within complex organizations.
  • Experience in insurance, banking, investment management, or financial services is highly desirable.
  • Strong expertise in operating model redesign, business process reengineering, digital transformation, and organizational change.
  • Demonstrated experience managing large transformation portfolios, budgets, executive stakeholders, and multidisciplinary teams.
  • Strong financial management, strategic planning, governance, and benefits realization capabilities.
  • Certifications such as PgMP, PMP, Prosci Change Management, Lean Six Sigma, TOGAF, or equivalent are advantageous.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Achievement of enterprise transformation strategy and strategic milestones.
  • Percentage of transformation programmes delivered within approved budgets and timelines.
  • Financial benefits realized through cost savings, revenue growth, and productivity improvements.
  • Return on investment (ROI) from enterprise transformation initiatives.
  • Improvement in operational efficiency and business performance.
  • Successful implementation of new operating models and business processes.
  • Digital adoption and technology modernization success rates.
  • Employee engagement, organizational readiness, and change adoption.
  • Customer experience and service delivery improvements.
  • Reduction in operational, technology, and regulatory risks.
  • Executive and board-level stakeholder satisfaction.

Lead Penetration Tester

Location: Remote (United States)
Reporting to: Director of Cybersecurity

At STN, we don't just adapt to the digital future, we engineer it. Our mission is to help organizations thrive in a rapidly evolving technology landscape through strategic insight, cutting-edge solutions, and a security-first mindset. We provide end-to-end services spanning cloud consulting, AI infrastructure, and enterprise security, enabling secure, scalable, and future-ready transformation.

As trusted advisors, we align IT investments with business outcomes that drive performance and growth, starting with deep strategic engagement and delivering tailored solutions built for long-term impact.

Our approach is innovation-led and rooted in cybersecurity, with a focus on leveraging the right technologies to solve real-world challenges. We invest in our people and foster a culture of growth, inclusion, and purpose because we believe empowered teams build transformative technology.

Overview
STN One is hiring a Lead Penetration Tester to plan and execute technically deep, authorized assessments across enterprise networks, applications, identity systems, and cloud environments. You will lead engagements from scoping and rules of engagement through exploitation, reporting, and retesting, while helping establish repeatable standards for STN's penetration-testing services.

Key Responsibilities

Penetration Testing & Security Requirements
  • Lead internal and external network penetration tests, Active Directory assessments, and identity-focused attack-path analysis.
  • Test web applications, APIs, cloud services, and exposed infrastructure using manual techniques supported by appropriate tooling.
  • Demonstrate realistic impact through controlled exploitation, privilege escalation, lateral movement, and chained findings when expressly authorized in the rules of engagement.
  • Define scope, assumptions, test prerequisites, communications plans, stop conditions, evidence handling, and safe-testing constraints before execution.
Security Architecture & Vulnerability Analysis
  • Support STN and customer security architecture improvements by validating segmentation, firewall exposure, identity pathways, and security monitoring outcomes through scoped adversarial testing.
  • Assess modern AI-enabled applications and agentic/MCP integrations where authorized, with emphasis on realistic abuse paths, privilege boundaries, and impact validation.
  • Evaluate segmentation, identity boundaries, configuration weaknesses, and detection/response visibility, then connect findings to practical business risk.
Technical Reporting & Remediation
  • Provide clear, reproducible technical evidence and prioritized remediation guidance without unnecessarily exposing sensitive customer data.
  • Write executive and technical reports, present results to customer leadership and engineers, and validate remediation through targeted retests.
Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Review junior tester work, mentor teammates, improve methodologies, maintain tooling, and support quality assurance across engagements.
  • Partner with DFIR, SOC, infrastructure, and internal STN teams to convert offensive insights into better controls and detections.

Experience & Qualifications

Required
  • 6+ years in hands-on penetration testing, red teaming, or offensive security, with independently led enterprise engagements.
  • Strong expertise in Active Directory attack paths, Windows/Linux exploitation, common network protocols, web/API vulnerabilities, and post-exploitation tradecraft.
  • Ability to distinguish real exploitable conditions from scanner findings and to demonstrate impact safely and ethically.
  • Fluency with offensive tools and scripting (for example, Burp Suite, Nmap, Python/PowerShell) and sound evidence documentation.
  • Experience developing rules of engagement, working within approved scope, and delivering high-quality reports to technical and executive audiences.
  • A current, recognized hands-on offensive-security certification such as OSCP/OSCP+, OSEP, GXPN, CRTO, or an equivalently practical advanced credential.
Preferred
  • Experience assessing Azure/AWS identity and cloud attack paths, Kubernetes, AI applications, LLM systems, or agent/MCP integrations.
  • Background designing red-team scenarios or purple-team exercises with SOC detection validation.
  • Evidence of method development, mentoring, technical writing, or building an offensive-security practice.

Compensation

  • Full-Time, Exempt
  • $145,000-$185,000/year, DOE

Benefits

  • Health Coverage – Medical, Dental & Vision
  • FSA Health and Dependent Care available
  • 401(k) Plan
  • Unlimited Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Observed Holidays Paid
  • Cell Phone Allowance
  • Collaborative, growth-driven culture
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the US. STN is unable to provide employment visa sponsorship for this position.

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and reference verification. All applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

Around 60% of your time goes to hands-on work in proofs of concept and customer projects, and the rest to presales, discovery and advisory for new and existing customers.   • Drive Data & AI business opportunities: contribute to business development by identifying opportunities, understanding client needs, and proposing data platform and AI solutions built on Databricks, Snowflake or Microsoft Fabric;
  • Tailor client-focused solutions: partner with sales teams to deliver technical presentations, demonstrations and RFP responses that show clients the value of the proposed architecture;
  • Lead discovery and shape solutions: lead the Discovery Workshops with new and existing clients to collect the business requirements, and work with the BA/PO to document them;
  • Design operational-fit architectures: analyse the use cases the platform has to serve (e.g. pipelines for BI, machine learning models, AI agents on governed company data) and design the end-to-end architecture, from ingestion to AI consumption;
  • Offer technical advisory: guide clients through platform and tool selection, explain the reasoning behind each choice, and pitch the end-to-end solution to internal and customer stakeholders;
  • Estimate cost and value: align business goals with the technology solution and propose practical models to calculate the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), including platform consumption and LLM usage;
  • Implement PoCs: build the PoCs behind the high-level solution designs yourself, on both the data and the AI side;
  • Technical leadership: lead the mid-senior data and AI engineers in turning the PoC into the production MVP, and stay involved in the customer project as the architecture evolves.

Must have:

  • 7+ years of experience in data engineering, ML engineering or AI engineering, covering lakehouses, pipelines, ETL/ELT processes and data governance;
  • 3+ years of experience in a Solutions Architect or Technical Lead role, leading the design and implementation of data or AI solutions;
  • Hands-on expertise in at least one of the following data platforms: Databricks, Snowflake or Microsoft Fabric;
  • Strong hands-on skills in at least one of the following AI areas, delivered on top of a data platform:
    • Agentic AI: LLM-based solutions using RAG, tool calling and MCP, agent orchestration (e.g. LangGraph, Databricks Agent Bricks, Snowflake Cortex), evaluation and guardrails;
    • Classical machine learning: feature engineering, model training and serving (e.g. scikit-learn, XGBoost, PyTorch), and MLOps with MLflow, feature stores and model monitoring;
  • Proficiency in data processing and orchestration tools (Apache Spark, Kafka, dbt, Airflow or the platform-native equivalents);
  • Strong knowledge of security & governance (RBAC, encryption, data catalogs and lineage, GDPR and EU AI Act compliance) and open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Parquet);
  • Experience with at least one cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP), IaC tools (Terraform or Bicep), CI/CD and observability for data and AI workloads;
  • Strong skills in Python and SQL for building data transformations and performance-optimized models (star schema, data vault);
  • Pre-sales experience, including RFPs, technical proposals, estimations and business development support;
  • Strong communication & leadership skills, with the ability to engage technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience with a second data platform from the list above;
  • Working knowledge of the AI area that is not your main strength (agentic AI or classical machine learning);
  • Experience with cloud AI services (e.g. Microsoft Foundry, Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker, Google Vertex AI);
  • A plus are the following certifications: Databricks Certified Data Engineer Professional or Generative AI Engineer Associate, SnowPro Advanced: Architect, Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate, or a cloud architect certification (Azure, AWS, GCP).

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive - Special District - Water & Utilities (West)
jobs.excerpt: The Company Serving the People Who Serve the People Granicus is driven by the excitement of building, implementing, and maintaining technology that is transforming the Govtech industry by bringing governments and its constituents together.
jobs.description:
The Company

Serving the People Who Serve the People

Granicus is driven by the excitement of building, implementing, and maintaining technology that is transforming the Govtech industry by bringing governments and its constituents together. We are on a mission to support our customers with meeting the needs of their communities and implementing our technology in ways that are equitable and inclusive. Granicus has consistently appeared on the GovTech 100 list over the past 5 years and has been recognized as the best companies to work on BuiltIn.

Over the last 25 years, we have served 5,500 federal, state, and local government agencies and more than 300 million citizen subscribers power an unmatched Subscriber Network that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place. With comprehensive cloud-based solutions for communications, government website design, meeting and agenda management software, records management, and digital services, Granicus empowers stronger relationships between government and residents across the U.S., U.K., Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By simplifying interactions with residents, while disseminating critical information, Granicus brings governments closer to the people they serve—driving meaningful change for communities around the globe.

Want to know more? See more of what we do here.

Job Summary

The Opportunity – Enterprise Account Executive, Water & Utilities (West):

Water and power districts are some of the largest and most essential Special Districts in the country, and the West is where the pressure on them is highest. Western water and public power agencies are managing drought and conservation programs, wildfire risk and power shutoff communications, aging infrastructure, water-quality rules, and rate increases that must be explained to customers and approved in public. Every one of those challenges runs through public meetings, public records, and clear communication with the community, which is exactly where Granicus helps.

As the Enterprise Account Executive for Water & Utilities West, you are the senior seller for the largest water, wastewater, and public power districts across 19 western states, supported by an assigned Business Development Representative, a Solution Consultant, and Granicus product overlays and specialty teams. Your book includes agencies such as large regional water wholesalers, municipal utility districts, and public power districts serving millions of customers. You will set the territory strategy and lead the largest, most complex pursuits: 12-to-18-month cycles that run through RFPs, board approvals, and multi-stakeholder buying committees.

This is a platform role, not a point-solution role. Granicus wins its largest deals by selling the Government Experience Cloud as one connected platform, tied to the agency's business outcomes. You will build multi-product deals across the full solution set that raise deal size, deepen adoption, and expand over time:

• Communications and engagement: govDelivery outreach by email and text, plus EngagementHQ for community input. Critical for conservation campaigns, outage and emergency alerts, and rate change notices.

• Agenda and meeting management: OneMeeting, Peak, Legistar, Boards and Commissions, and meeting video, for open, transparent board meetings.

• Websites: govAccess and OpenCities: accessible, mobile-friendly websites for customers and the public.

• Service Cloud and digital services: govService, OneView, and OpenForms for online requests,forms, payments, and workflow.

• Public records: GovQA for public records requests and govRecords for official records.

• PCL (permitting, compliance, and licensing): AMANDA and SmartGov for permits, inspections,licensing, and code compliance.

• AI, intelligence, and services: GXA, the Government Experience Agent, answering customer questions around the clock from approved agency content; GXI for experience analytics; and Customer Experience Services.

Inspiration:

We grow at Granicus by hiring the world-class sales talent that we are deserving of. We only hire the absolute best of the best - those who can demonstrate that they've done is successfully and consistently throughout their sales careers. We seek those who are hungry and humble - that embody continued learning, and role mastery with the belief that large attainment is built through daily persistence and action. As one barometer of this, we seek those who have consistently earned President's Club recognition in their last 5 years; 4 or 5 great! 3 times, maybe. 2 times, likely not. 0-1 times, pass. A+ results are achieved through A+ teams. We never settle.

This is a builder's role. You will be the first enterprise seller dedicated to western water and utilities, and you will partner directly with the Special Districts Manager to roll out the vertical go-to-market strategy and the sales playbooks the team runs on, defining how Granicus wins in this market rather than inheriting a finished playbook. If you want to become the recognized expert in western water and power, and you are energized by long, consultative enterprise cycles with real community impact, this is the seat.

Your Territory at a Glance:

• Territory: Enterprise water and utility districts (about $12M or more in annual revenue) in Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Kansas, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oregon, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming.

• Book: About 530 enterprise accounts. California is the largest concentration, followed by Texas, Washington, and Colorado.

• Primary verticals: Water and wastewater; multi-function water and utility districts (municipal utility districts, river authorities, community choice aggregators); retail public power; and natural gas utility districts.

• Secondary verticals: Irrigation and water resources, flood control and stormwater, and solid waste and recycling, worked through targeted plays after the primary book.

• Deal profile: Multi-product platform sales across Granicus cloud solutions, with average first-year deals of about $175K and 12-to-18-month cycles with board approval.

• Annual quota: Projected at $1.0M to $1.2M in new ARR per year.

• Team: An assigned BDR and Solution Consultant, plus Granicus product overlays and specialty teams. Mid-market and smaller utilities will be covered by additional sellers as the team grows.

• Location: Remote, based in the western United States (Pacific or Mountain time preferred), with travel up to30%. Proximity to California is a plus.

About Granicus:

For more than 25 years, Granicus has helped public sector organizations strengthen constituent relationships, modernize service delivery, and increase transparency. Thousands of government organizations rely on our cloud platform for communications and engagement, digital services, websites, meeting and agenda management, public records, and operational efficiency. We are driven by a simple idea: serving the people who serve the people.

About the Special Districts Team:

There are more than 50,000 Special District government entities in the United States, and Granicus actively serves more than 30 types of Special District markets. The Special Districts team is organized byvertical, not by geography alone: each seller develops deep expertise in the industries it serves, so that every customer conversation starts with an understanding of how that district is governed, funded,regulated, and measured. Each seller is assigned one or two of the following priority verticals and goes deep on them:

• Transportation and transit agencies • Water, wastewater, and sanitation districts • Public utilities and community energy agencies • Healthcare and hospital districts • Housing authorities • Airport and port authorities • Fire districts and emergency services agencies • Parks and recreation districts • Other independent special-purpose governments

This seat focuses on water, wastewater, and public utilities across the western United States, alongside a peer enterprise seller covering the East. Our goal is not to sell software. It is to become the partner these organizations call when they need to engage customers, run more transparent meetings, modernize operations, or deliver services digitally.

What You Will Own:

Revenue and territory strategy: • Own the enterprise number for Water & Utilities West: net-new ARR from new logos plus expansion within existing water and utility customers.

• Build and execute an annual territory plan and named-account plans for your largest agencies that map the path to quota, and revise them quarterly against pipeline reality.

• Prioritize a large, multi-state book: focus outbound on the primary verticals and the largest agencies, and use targeted plays for secondary verticals and inbound.

• Maintain pipeline coverage sufficient to support consistent attainment, with an accurate, defensible forecast in Salesforce.

Pipeline generation: • Self-source a meaningful share of your own pipeline. The BDR accelerates you; they do not replace your prospecting.

• Run multi-channel outbound (phone, email, LinkedIn, referrals, partners) and work the western water and power calendar: ACWA, CSDA, CMUA, AWWA and its western sections, APPA, and state rural water and utility associations.

• Turn market presence into pipeline: relationships with engineering and rate consultants, channel partners, and association leaders should produce warm introductions, not just conference badges.

Complex enterprise sales cycles: • Lead opportunities from first discovery through procurement, legal negotiation, board approval, and signature.

• Navigate public procurement with confidence: RFPs and RFIs, cooperative purchasing vehicles, committee reviews, and public board votes.

• Quarterback the pursuit team (Solution Consultant, product overlays and specialty teams, Product, Marketing, Customer Success, and Sales Leadership) around a single account strategy. You own the relationship, qualification, business outcomes, and close plan; your partners own their areas of expertise.

Enterprise selling disciplines: • Multithreading. Build relationships across the agency, from the general manager and board to IT, communications, the clerk's office, and customer service. No deal rests on a single contact.

• Differentiation. Show clearly why Granicus, and why now, against competitors, homegrown tools, and doing nothing, using proof from peer agencies.

• ROI and business cases. Build executive-level business cases and ROI analyses tied to outcomes a utility's general manager and board already care about: customer trust, rate-case transparency, conservation results, outage and emergency communication, and operational efficiency.

• Mutual action plans. Agree a mutual action plan with every enterprise customer, mapping each step from discovery through procurement, legal review, and board approval, with owners and dates on both sides.

Platform and cloud selling: • Lead with the platform. Position Granicus as a connected set of cloud solutions tied to the agency's priorities, not as a single product that answers one RFP line item.

• Build multi-product deals from the first discovery call: map the agency's problems across communications, meetings, websites, Service Cloud, records, PCL, and GXA, and size the opportunity to match.

• Grow deal size and customer value over time with a land-and-expand plan for every account, so a first purchase becomes a platform relationship.

• Bring in product overlays and specialty teams for each cloud at the right moment while keeping ownership of the overall solution, the business case, and the close.

Market expertise and executive relationships:

• Become the go-to expert in western water and public power: how districts are governed and funded, rate-setting and public notice requirements (such as Proposition 218 in California), open meeting laws, drought and conservation programs, wildfire mitigation, and water-quality regulation.

• Build trusted relationships with General Managers, Assistant General Managers, CIOs and IT Directors, Public Affairs and Communications Directors, Board Secretaries and Clerks, and customer service leaders.

• Bring insight to every conversation. Customers should leave meetings with you knowing more about their market than when they walked in.

• Represent Granicus at western water and power conferences and association meetings as a credible industry voice.

GTM build-out and Internal Leadership: • Partner with the Special Districts Manager to roll out the Water & Utilities GTM strategy for the West (ideal customer profiles, messaging, plays, and enablement) and feed what you learn in the field back into the playbooks.

• Serve as the senior seller and owning responsibility with pipeline generation, account penetration, forecast accuracy, and total revenue, and directing the work of your assigned BDR and Solution Consultant.

• Run joint account planning and opportunity reviews; coach teammates through complex cycles and pull them into enterprise pursuits where it develops them.

• Set the tone: collaborative, transparent, accountable. Performance is measured on your individual contribution and being a strong cultural fit.

What Your Impact Will Look Like

Who You Are:

Skills and experience get you in the door. These qualities are what we hire for, and what separates the sellers who win in this market:

• Elite credibility builder. You build credibility fast with agencies that have never worked with Granicus. Net-new general managers and boards see you as an industry expert, a trusted advisor, and a problem solver, not a vendor.

• Relentless work ethic. You bring elite effort every day: the preparation, the outreach, and the follow-through, whether or not anyone is watching.

• Prospects every day. You prospect every day, in good quarters and bad. Pipeline is a daily habit,not a campaign.

• Elite curiosity. You ask the next question, then the one after that. You want to know how anagency really works, what keeps its general manager up at night, and why a deal is stuck.

• High emotional intelligence. You read the room, adjust to each stakeholder, and build real relationships with board members, staff, and your own teammates.

• Focused. You ignore internal and external noise (reorganizations, competitor chatter, a lost deal, a slow quarter) and stay on the work that moves the number.

• Growth-oriented and coachable. You seek feedback, act on it quickly, and keep studying both the craft of selling and the industry you serve.

• Wins every day. You set a high daily standard and meet it. Winning each day is how you hit the year.

What You Bring:

Required:

• 8+ years of enterprise SaaS sales running complex enterprise sales cycles, with a documented record of exceeding quota in multi-stakeholder environments.

• Experience owning 12-to-18-month enterprise cycles that involve formal procurement (RFPs,cooperative contracts, public board approval).

• Experience selling into water, wastewater, energy, or other utilities, or into the public sector or a similarly regulated industry.

• A track record of platform selling: closing multi-product or multi-cloud deals at higher deal sizes than single point-solution sales, and working alongside product overlays and specialists without handing them the deal.

• Demonstrated mastery of enterprise selling disciplines: multithreading, differentiation, ROI and business cases, and mutual action plans.

• Proven ability to build territory and account plans and to self-generate pipeline through outbound and market engagement.

• Fluency in consultative, value-based selling and in building executive business cases and ROI models.

• Executive presence and communication skills strong enough to credibly engage a General Manager, a CIO, and an elected board in the same week.

• A track record of leading cross-functional pursuit teams and of working well alongside BDRs, other AEs, Solution Consultants, and Customer Success.

• Disciplined Salesforce hygiene and forecasting; based in the western United States and willing to travel up to 30%, including regular travel in California.

Bonus points: • Direct experience working for, selling to, or consulting with water districts, municipal utility districts, or public power utilities.

• Existing relationships with water and power agencies in California,Washington, Colorado,or the Mountain West.

• Familiarity with utility customer communications and technology: customer information and billing systems, outage and emergency notification, conservation programs, and customer self service.

• Experience helping stand up a new vertical, segment, or sales motion — building playbooks rather than only running them.

• Familiarity with GovTech categories Granicus plays in: constituent engagement and communications, websites and CMS, meeting and agenda management, digital service delivery, and government operations.

• Working knowledge of Special District governance and public-sector budgeting cycles.

• Active membership in western water and power associations such as ACWA, CSDA, CMUA, AWWA, or APPA.

You Will Love This Job If You Have

What Success Looks Like:

The Enterprise AEs who thrive here are students of their market first and salespeople second. They know how a water district's rate study and public hearing work, why a public power board's wildfire mitigation plan matters, and how a drought declaration changes what customers need to hear, and they use that knowledge to steer conversations toward transparency, customer engagement, and operational modernization rather than product features. They sell the platform, not a product: they connect an agency's problems across departments and build deals that grow. They earn trust by being useful, and they close because customers believe they understand the problem.

If you are energized by learning an industry deeply, building executive relationships from scratch, and being the person who defines how Granicus wins in a market, you will do well in this role.

Why This Role Matters:

Water and power districts keep taps running and lights on for millions of people across the West. Helping them communicate clearly during droughts, wildfires, and rate changes, run open and transparent meetings, and deliver services digitally has a direct, visible impact on the communities they serve. This role sits at the center of that impact, for Granicus, for its customers, and for the communities behind them.

Our Hiring Process:

We keep the process focused and respectful of your time. Expect six steps:

• 1. HR screen: a conversation with our Talent team about your background, sales track record, the role, and compensation.

• 2. Behavioral and personality assessment: a short online assessment of how you work, communicate, and handle pressure.

• 3. Writing assignment: a short written exercise that shows how you think and how you communicate with a utility executive.

• 4. Hiring Manager interview (90 minutes): a deep discussion of your enterprise selling experience, public-sector track record, platform deals, and how you would build the Water & Utilities West territory.

• 5. Panel assessment exercise (90 minutes): a western water or utility district scenario, presented to a panel of sales leaders as you would to a customer's executive team.

• 6. Final interview with the Segment Leader: a conversation on strategy, fit, and the mandate for this role.

Posted Compensation:• Base salary: S120,000-$140,000 • On-target earnings (OTE): $240,000 to $280,000 at 100% of quota (base plus target commission).

Final compensation has flexibility and depends on experience, location, and skills. This role is also eligible for Granicus benefits.

Pay Range

USD $110,000.00 - USD $130,000.00 /Yr.

About Us

Don’t have all the skills/experience mentioned above? At Granicus, we are trying to build diverse, inclusive teams. We do not have degree requirements for most of our roles. If you don’t meet every requirement above but are excited to learn more, we encourage you to apply. We might just be able to find another role that could be a perfect fit!

Security and Privacy Requirements

  • Responsible for Granicus information security by appropriately preserving the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) of Granicus information assets in accordance with the company's information security program.
  • Responsible for ensuring the data privacy of our employees and customers, their data, as well as taking all required privacy training in a timely manner, in accordance with company policies.

The Team

  • We are a remote-first company with a globally distributed workforce across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, India, Armenia, Australia, and New Zealand.

The Culture

  • At Granicus, we are building a transparent, inclusive, and safe space for everyone who wants to bea part of our journey.
  • A few culture highlights include – Employee Resource Groups to encourage diverse voices
  • Coffee with Mark sessions – Our employees get to interact with our CEO on very important andsometimes difficult issues ranging from mental health to work-life balance and current affairs.
  • Microsoft Teams communities focused on wellness, art, furbabies, family, parenting, and more.
  • We bring in special guests from time to time to discuss issues that impact our employeepopulation

The Impact

  • We are proud to serve dynamic organizations around the globe that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place — quite literally. We have so many powerful success stories that illustrate how our solutions are impacting the world. See more of our impact here.

The Benefits

At Granicus, we offer a comprehensive and flexible benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance—starting from day one. Here’s what you can expect as a U.S.-based team member:

Flexibility & Balance

  • Flexible Time Off – Take the time you need to rest, recharge, and live your life.
  • Company-Wide Wellbeing Days – Paid days off to unplug and focus on your mental health.
  • Work From Home Reimbursement – Support a productive home office environment.
Health & Wellness
  • Multiple Health Plan Options – Including a 100% employer-paid plan.
  • Employer HSA Contributions – When enrolled in a High-Deductible Health Plan.
  • Fitness Reimbursement Program – Stay active, your way.
  • On-Demand Mental Health Support – Access to Headspace and other wellness tools.
Family & Future
  • Paid Parental Leave – For both birthing and non-birthing parents.
  • Traditional & Roth 401(k) – With a generous company match.
  • Life & AD&D Insurance – 100% employer-paid coverage for peace of mind.
Growth & Recognition
  • Online Learning Platforms – Fuel your professional development.
  • Competitive Salary & Bonuses – Your contributions are valued and rewarded.

Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Director of Recruiting and Development
jobs.excerpt: Segal McCambridge, a nationally recognized litigation defense firm, is seeking an experienced and strategic Director of Recruiting & Development to lead the firm's nationwide recruiting, attorney development, and retention initiatives.
jobs.description:
Segal McCambridge, a nationally recognized litigation defense firm, is seeking an experienced and strategic Director of Recruiting & Development to lead the firm's nationwide recruiting, attorney development, and retention initiatives.

Reporting directly to the Firm's Managing Shareholder, this highly visible leadership role will have the opportunity to shape the firm's talent strategy and play an integral part in its continued growth and success. The Director will oversee all aspects of recruitment across the firm's nationwide offices, including lateral partners, associates, law students, and professional staff, while developing programs designed to attract exceptional talent, strengthen attorney development, and foster long-term retention.

This is an exciting opportunity for a recruiting or law firm administration professional who understands the legal industry, enjoys building relationships, and wants to make a meaningful impact on the future of a growing national law firm. This position may be based remotely or in any of Segal McCambridge's offices nationwide.

Key Responsibilities

Nationwide Recruiting & Talent Acquisition

  • Lead and manage the full life-cycle recruiting process across all firm offices and practice areas, including lateral partners, associates, law students, and non-attorney professionals.
  • Partner with Office Managing Shareholders, firm leadership, and Human Resources to identify staffing needs, develop targeted candidate profiles, and establish recruiting priorities.
  • Design and implement innovative recruiting strategies to attract top legal talent and support the firm's growth objectives.
  • Oversee candidate sourcing, resume screening, initial candidate assessments, interview coordination, and offer development in collaboration with hiring shareholders and HR.
  • Partner with Marketing, HR, and hiring managers to develop compelling job postings and recruitment materials for the firm's website and external job boards.
  • Develop and oversee a law school recruiting program focused on internships and entry-level attorney recruitment.
  • Build and maintain relationships with law schools, career services offices, and other legal recruiting networks nationwide.
  • Manage relationships with outside legal recruiting firms and serve as the primary point of contact for recruitment agency inquiries.
  • Monitor recruiting effectiveness and identify opportunities to improve processes, candidate experience, and hiring outcomes.
  • Mentor and develop a recruiting coordinator.

Attorney Development & Retention

  • Develop and implement firmwide attorney development initiatives, including training, mentorship, professional development, and career advancement programs.
  • Establish regular communication with associates to assess job satisfaction, career goals, engagement, and potential retention concerns.
  • Partner with Office Managing Shareholders and practice group leaders to identify associate development needs and opportunities for improvement.
  • Identify high-performing associates and help establish career paths and opportunities for advancement, including progression toward shareholder leadership.
  • Serve as a liaison between associate committees, firm leadership, and management to identify and address firmwide associate concerns and priorities.
  • Evaluate associate feedback and recommendations, identify trends, and present actionable recommendations to firm management.
  • Develop and implement retention strategies and incentive programs in collaboration with HR and firm leadership, including referral incentives and recognition initiatives.
  • Partner with local offices to coordinate associate engagement activities and professional development events.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen firm culture, collaboration, professional satisfaction, and long-term attorney retention.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • Minimum of 7 years of experience in recruiting, talent acquisition, or administration within a law firm environment.
  • Prior experience recruiting attorneys, including lateral partners and associates.
  • Demonstrated understanding of law firm operations, attorney staffing needs, and the legal recruiting landscape.
  • Experience developing and implementing recruiting strategies, professional development initiatives, and employee retention programs.
  • Strong relationship-building, communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and manage competing priorities across multiple offices.
  • Highly ethical, discreet, and capable of handling sensitive and confidential personnel matters.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
  • Juris Doctor (J.D.) is preferred but not required.

Compensation & Benefits

The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $175,000–$225,000, depending on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors.

Segal McCambridge recognizes that our people are essential to our success. We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Health savings account (HSA)
  • Flexible spending account (FSA)
  • Life insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Parental leave
  • Employee assistance program
  • Employee discount program

About Segal McCambridge

Founded in 1986, Segal McCambridge has grown from a four-attorney Chicago practice into a nationally recognized litigation defense firm with nearly four decades of experience representing and defending clients in complex litigation.

With offices across the country, Segal McCambridge represents Fortune 500 companies, corporations, and individuals in a broad range of litigation matters. Our practice areas include asbestos and toxic tort litigation, class actions, construction, employment, environmental matters, insurance coverage and bad faith, life sciences, product liability, professional liability, technology and cyber risk, transportation, and warranty litigation.

Our attorneys are committed to delivering sophisticated litigation counsel and effective advocacy. We value professionals who share our commitment to excellence, teamwork, and exceptional client service.

Join Our Team

At Segal McCambridge, we recognize that attracting, developing, and retaining exceptional talent is fundamental to our continued success. The Director of Recruiting & Development will have a unique opportunity to work directly with firm leadership, influence firmwide strategy, and help shape the next chapter of our growth.

If you are a strategic recruiting or law firm administration professional who is passionate about developing talent and building successful teams, we invite you to explore this opportunity with Segal McCambridge.

Salary: $175,000 – $225,000 / year

jobs.description:
LanguageLine Solutions is Hiring!

At LanguageLine, we strive for a world in which language and cultural barriers no longer exist. Use your language skills to dramatically improve the lives of limited-English speakers, as well as the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing. Even better, you can do this while working from your own home.

LanguageLine has been certified as a Great Place to Work, and is regularly listed as one of America’s top work-from-home employers.

Our interpreters serve clients across numerous industries, including health care, 911, first responders, education, government agencies, and all walks of business.

As an interpreter, you will receive training that is the best in the industry. We’ll ensure that you learn new skills while further developing your skillset. We provide numerous opportunities for advancement. You’ll be in a certified ASTM and ISO environment. You'll also be supported by a Senior Language Specialist, as well as our Interpreter and Technology Help Desks.

Join our team now!

Job Description

Work at Home Bilingual Wodaabe-English Phone Interpreter


Job Title: Wodaabe Interpreter

Location: Work at Home position in United States

Position: Phone Interpreter

Status: Independent Contractor

Pay: $0.75 - $0.90 per minute


We Offer:

  • Employee Referral Program.
  • Advancement opportunities within the organization.
  • Interpreter support.
  • An inclusive and diverse work environment.
  • **This is an independent contractor position and therefore not eligible for employee benefits.**

Position Overview:


The Wodaabe Telephone Interpreter is responsible for handling calls on demand, and renders the meaning of conversations between Wodaabeand English speakers. The interpreter breaks the communication barrier in a wide range of industries that LanguageLine Solutions serves: Healthcare, Government, Insurance, Financial, Utilities, Travel & Hospitality, General Business, Law Enforcement, Court, and 911.


The interpreter processes information quickly, concisely and recognizes sensitive cultural differences. The interpreter is professional and courteous at all times and uses appropriate terminology and understands common industry procedures and practices. The interpreting sessions may involve simple or complex, technical or non-technical subjects.


This position does not involve written translation however translators and other skilled linguists are encouraged to apply. The Interpreters translate verbally.


**This is a remote position. The Interpreter works from his/her home-office. It is essential to ensure a quiet & secure environment.**


Essential Job Functions

  • Respond to the interpreting sessions promptly and conduct interpretation in a friendly and professional manner.
  • Render correct concepts and meanings according to the conventions of established interpretation protocol, avoiding omissions or additions.
  • Speak clearly in both languages using proper pronunciation, enunciation and polite expressions.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor throughout the interpreting sessions at all times.
  • Remain calm during interpreting sessions in the event that one of the primary speakers is incoherent or upset, especially in emergency situations such as 911 calls.
  • Maintain punctuality and availability during work hours.
  • Follow client instructions, in compliance with protocol to ensure client expectations are met with the Limited English-speaking Person (LEP), avoiding interaction with the LEP without client’s permission.
  • Understand protocol and terminology for various industries including, but not limited to, Medical, Insurance, Finance and Law.
  • Demonstrate commitment to cultural sensitivity and working in a diverse environment.
  • **Some calls may be highly emotional and/or stressful in nature. The interpreter may need to remain on a call for extended periods without breaks due to the nature of the call or may, at times experience high call volumes. The interpreter must have the ability to provide the required, company standards of service within this dynamic environment. **

Qualifications

  • Fluency inWodaabe and English and skilled in the associated cultural dynamics.
  • Ability to provide cultural competency and assess regional and accent differences to find ways of communicating with the LEP.
  • Excellent listening, retention and note-taking skills to maintain a high level of accuracy during interpretation.
  • Ability to concentrate, stay detached from the conversation, remain neutral and objective at all times, and remain on calls that involve sensitive subjects such as end of life conversations, pregnancy termination, vaccinations, and matters concerning sexual orientation and/or gender expression.
  • Education or work experience in language-related fields such as teaching, language assessment, translation or interpretation preferred.
  • Must be able to adapt to any LLS technology enhancements that improve service delivery and meet client demands.
  • Must be at least 18 years of age.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States
  • Applicants for employment in the US must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States and with LanguageLine Solutions (i.e., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant status).
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Candidates who are currently employed by a client of LanguageLine Solutions or an affiliated LanguageLine Solutions business may not be eligible for consideration.
  • Ability to read and write the requested languages - highly preferred.

**Based on your location, a post-offer, a pre-employment background check and/or drug screen may be required**


Technical Requirements:

  • Dedicated personal device for business purposes.
    • Desktop / Laptop Computers with any of the following Operating Systems: Windows, MacOS, or ChromeOS.
    • Tablets (iPadOS or Android) are acceptable.
    • Smartphones (iOS or Android) are also acceptable.
  • Restricted brands:
    • Kaspersky products.
    • Huawei hardware.
  • High speed Internet connection for work related electronic communication. This internet connection should provide download speeds of no less than 5 Mbps, upload speeds of 3 Mbps, Ping value of no more than 300 ms, Jitter value of no more than 30 ms.
  • Must have access to a quiet space free from background noise or distraction.

Physical Requirements:

  • Must be able to operate a keyboard and mouse and remain in a stationary position in front of a computer the majority of the workday.
  • Must be able to operate company provided software and systems to perform all aspects of the job.
  • Must have sufficient manual dexterity to type or write.
  • Able to lift up to 26 lbs.
  • May be exposed to moderate noise levels; i.e. computer, audio, telephone.

Applications will be accepted for one hundred eighty (180) days from the posting date of November 18, 2026.

United by one profound purpose: to reach EVERY PATIENT POSSIBLE. At Avalere Health, we ensure every patient is identified, treated, supported, and cared for. Equally. Our Advisory, Medical, and Marketing teams come together – powerfully and intentionally – to forge unconventional connections, building a future where healthcare is not a barrier and no patient is left behind.
Achieving our mission starts with providing enriching, purpose-driven careers for our team that empower them to make a tangible impact on patient lives. We are committed to creating a culture where our employees are empowered to bring their whole selves to work and tap into the power of diverse backgrounds and skillsets to play a part in making a difference for every patient, everywhere.
Our flexible approach to working allows our global teams to decide where they want to work, whether in-office or at home based on team and client need. Major city hubs in London, Manchester, Washington, D.C., and New York, and smaller offices globally, serve as collaboration hubs allowing our teams to come together when it matters. Homeworkers are equally supported, with dedicated social opportunities and resources.
Our inclusive culture is at the heart of everything we do. We proudly support our employees in bringing their whole selves to work with our six Employee Network Groups – Diverse Ability, Family, Gender, LGBTQ+, Mental Health, and Race/Ethnicity. These groups provide opportunities to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion and to connect, learn, and socialise through regular meetings and programs of activity. We are an accredited Fertility Friendly employer with our Fertility Policy, enhanced parental leave, and culture of flexibility ensuring every employee feels supported across their family planning journey and can work in a way that suits their family’s needs.
We are deeply invested in supporting professional growth for our employees through day-to-day career experiences, access to thousands of on-demand training sessions, regular career conversations, and the opportunity for global, cross-capability career moves.
We take pride in being part of the Disability Confident Scheme. This helps make sure you can be interviewed fairly if you have a disability, long term health condition, or are neurodiverse. If you'd like to apply and need adjustments made, you can let us know in your application.

About the role:


We are seeking a VP, Engagement Strategy to shape how brands show up in the real world across the channels, touchpoints, behaviors, and moments that influence patient action. This role translates brand strategy into connected omnichannel experiences, ensuring content and messaging are not only strategically sound, but delivered in the right place, at the right time, in the right way. This individual will serve as the day-to-day engagement strategy lead for clients and internal teams, building strategies that connect audience insight, platform behavior, content, media, and measurement into experiences that drive engagement, affinity, and impact.

What you'll do:

  • Lead end-to-end engagement strategy across key accounts, owning direction, quality of output, and overall impact.
  • Translate brand strategy into omnichannel engagement plans, activation strategies, experience maps, content matrices, and channel-specific content guidance.
  • Lead engagement planning, activation, and measurement across patient journeys, ensuring strategies are grounded in audience needs, behaviors, and decision-making pathways.
  • Develop brand ecosystem and experience strategies that define how touchpoints, content, and channels work together across the full engagement journey.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Brand Strategy, Creative, Medical/Scientific, Media, Account, Analytics, and other teams to integrate strategy and bring engagement plans to life.
  • Apply platform, channel, and performance insights to optimize activations against defined success metrics.
  • Identify growth opportunities and innovative engagement approaches that improve audience connection, brand affinity, and business impact.
  • Manage, mentor, and develop senior and junior strategists, providing clear direction and feedback.

About you:

Vous avez de bonnes connaissances du processus de facturation et d’encaissement.

Vous disposez de très bonnes compétences en analyse de données et en interprétation d'informations financières.

Vous avez un excellente maîtrise des outils bureautiques, en particulier Excel (niveau avancé), BO avec la capacité de développer des outils automatisés et des macros.
