jobs.excerpt: PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here PATH is a global nonprofit advancing health innovations for the people who need them most.
jobs.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here

PATH is a global nonprofit advancing health innovations for the people who need them most. With 50 years of experience, a global team of experts, and trusted partnerships spanning 70+ countries, PATH turns breakthroughs into better health for millions every single year.


PATH’s Center for Vaccine Innovation and Access (CVIA) brings together our expertise across every stage of the long and complex process of vaccine research, development, and delivery to make lifesaving vaccines widely available to children and communities across the world. CVIA’s current portfolio encompasses more than two dozen vaccines either in development or already in use to protect against fifteen different diseases. Our focus is on vaccines to address the leading diseases that claim children’s lives worldwide: pneumonia, diarrheal disease, and malaria; as well as other global health priorities, such as polio and meningitis. We work in partnership with national health ministries, pharmaceutical manufacturers, donors, international financing and regulatory organizations, and many others. PATH has led numerous global partnerships, including the award-winning Meningitis Vaccine Project and the Malaria Vaccine Initiative, which helped develop the first malaria vaccine candidate recommended for pilot implementation.


PATH is recruiting for a Global Head, Center for Vaccine Innovation and Access (CVIA), hereafter referred to as Head of CVIA. The incumbent will be a strategic, thoughtful, and inspiring leader who will report to PATH’s Chief Scientific Officer (CSO), Product Development. The Head of CVIA will partner within and across PATH Divisions to enhance PATH’s commitment to accelerating health equity. The incumbent will have deep scientific and technical expertise in vaccine development needed to lead CVIA’s portfolio of product development and introduction and technical assistance (impact enabler) projects, which are focused on preventing and/or controlling infectious disease burden that disproportionately affect people in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).


The Head of CVIA is responsible for leading the development of strategy and high-level tactics, as well as the implementation of PATH’s vaccines and biologics research, development, and introduction activities, consistent with PATH’s mission, values, and policies, and CVIA’s goals and objectives. The Head of CVIA is an integral member of the PATH Product Development Leadership Team, in addition to leading the CVIA Leadership Team (CVIA LT). Given the ever-changing external public-private partnership environment, the Head of CVIA will serve as a change leader, strategy creator, proactive partner in developing comprehensive cross-disciplinary tactics, and an enabler of exceptional execution through both cross-disciplinary, matrixed product teams as well as teams more narrowly focused on technical assistance in one or more disciplines.


Responsibilities:

  • Evolve and oversee a robust and comprehensive program that supports innovation and partnership in vaccine and biologics research, development, and introduction.
  • Support Business Development and external partnerships/alliances including with the Gates Foundation, WHO and Gavi and newly emerging donors.
  • Establish strategic priorities for CVIA’s portfolio of activities and manage resource allocation across CVIA, in compliance with donor funding.
  • Ensure the implementation and reporting of CVIA’s portfolio, in alignment with existing contracts and partnership agreements.
  • Drive, organize, and lead PATH’s efforts to identify innovative mechanisms and approaches to develop new or improve existing vaccines and biologics, particularly for diseases of poverty and for products addressing “market failures”.
  • Create an organizational environment of collaboration, quality improvement, equity, innovation, and creative problem solving.
  • Identify opportunities to accelerate impact and/or lower development costs for new and/or improved existing vaccines.
  • Collaborate with external partners to advance vaccine and biologic candidates from discovery through clinical development and introduction.
  • Provide oversight for the portfolio of existing and emerging vaccines and biologics, with a focus on innovation across the product lifecycle to take to scale fit-for-purpose products in communities in low resource settings with the highest need.
  • Lead strategic and tactical analyses of vaccine technologies and assess candidates against a set of selection criteria that align with CVIA’s strategic plan and portfolio goals and objectives.
  • Present at scientific meetings and represent PATH and CVIA at international, regional and national meetings.
  • Ensure fit-for-purpose organizational structure and operating model for CVIA, including governance models that delegate responsibilities to the right level in the organization. Strive to create an organizational environment of collaboration, quality improvement, equity, innovation, and creative problem solving.
  • Serve on the Product Development Leadership Team, participate in the decision making of the Division across a variety of programs and functional areas, clearly communicate and collaborate with other global program and functional leaders at PATH and positively interact with the PATH Executive Team and other programmatic divisions.
  • Be prepared to supervise a portion of the CVIA portfolio as needed, directly mentoring and managing the relevant Project Leaders overseeing ongoing projects.

Required skills and experience:

  • Strategic thinker: demonstrated ability to be innovative and take prudent risks to ensure CVIA remains relevant and impactful, coupled with strong and dynamic leadership skills in managing, motivating, coordinating, and supporting all facets of PATH’s and CVIA’s strategic and operational plans and priorities.
  • Communications: precise, candid and engaging spokesperson who can effectively communicate PATH’s and CVIA’s scientific activities at a national, regional, and international level in the context of PATH’s mission.
  • Demonstrated ability to build relationships with diverse donors.
  • Technical: deep vaccine development experience.
  • Nimble learner: proven experience in active learning through experimentation when tackling new problems, using both successes and failures as learning fodder.
  • Decisively makes high-quality decisions, even when based on incomplete information or in the face of uncertainty, balancing between speed and quality.
  • Building partnerships and working collaboratively with others, including from other cultures and countries, to meet shared objectives.

Qualifications:

  • 20 years of experience in research, product development, and introduction of vaccines within the pharmaceutical industry or equivalent is required.
    • Experience with biologics is desirable but not required.
    • Pharmaceutical industry experience preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience in proposal writing and grant-based funding.
  • Proven experience in project team leadership of research, preclinical, clinical, regulatory, CMC, and/or quality assurance aspects of vaccine and related technology development.
  • 10-15 years of experience managing professional, scientific, and technical staff with an approach that is responsive to diverse work styles; experience managing managers desired. Strong leadership skills with the ability to set a strategic vision and direction and manage the staff to these core objectives
  • Demonstrated and proven track record understanding the needs and requirements for developing vaccine and/or biologic health solutions for low- and middle-income countries.
  • Demonstrated and proven experience working in a multi-site team-based organizational structure, including partners and other collaborators; developing-country experience a plus.
  • Experience working across multiple teams to problem solve collaboratively: facilitate discussions to troubleshoot issues, remove barriers and drive root cause analysis.
  • Proven ability to work in multilateral partnerships to influence and achieve results.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively (both written and verbal) across multiple functions, levels, and internal & external teams across multiple geographies.
  • Fluency in English.
  • Available to travel nationally and internationally at least 25 percent of the time.

Location:

  • Must have legal authorization to work in a country where PATH is registered.
  • Location of work needs to be compatible with a CVIA leadership team in multiple time zones including US (Eastern & Pacific Times) and Europe.
  • PATH operates within a hybrid workplace model. Hybrid employees reside within commuting distance of one of PATH offices. PATH’s US offices are located in Seattle, WA, and Washington, DC. This position is approved to be a remote employee where PATH is registered.

PATH is a diverse nonprofit organization that creates a culture of collaboration and partnership. Learn more about the impact you can make globally here.


We offer our employees a competitive salary and generous benefits. For candidates based in the U.S., the annual salary range for this position is $380,000-$420,000. The final salary is based on a variety of objective factors. PATH provides a comprehensive benefit package that includes 15 vacation, 11 holiday, 2 personal, and 12 sick days per year; medical and dental plans; life insurance; and disability and retirement benefits. What is Shotgun?

Shotgun is a leading platform dedicated to empowering live music event organizers and touring artists, driving the future of the live music industry. Our mission is to build the infrastructure that enables live music to thrive.

We provide powerful tools to sell tickets, build strong brands, and connect with fans in meaningful ways. From 2020 to 2025, Shotgun achieved rapid growth with GMV increasing 25× and revenue growing 40×, leading the company to profitability. Today, we support more than 10,000 clients and engage over 8,000,000 users across Europe, the US, and LATAM.

In the past seven years, Shotgun has raised €10M from Newfund, Venrex, One RagTime, Creator Collective, and BPI Culture Fund. We are a lean and dynamic team, with offices in Paris, Miami, São Paulo, Lisbon, and Marseille. Our culture is built on passion, commitment, ownership, and humility.

The Role

As Shotgun grows, so does the complexity behind every ticket sold. We're expanding into new countries and live music experiences, and our engineering teams need a platform that helps them move fast with confidence.

As our Engineering Manager Platform, your mission is to lead the team building the technical foundation for Shotgun’s next stage of growth. You own the Platform roadmap and technical choices across four pillars: observability, security, scalability, and developer experience.

You will manage a team of two Staff Software Engineers and one SRE, reporting to Vivien, our Head of Engineering. This is a hands-on role: expect to spend around 50% of your time on technical work and 50% on people management, team processes, and collaboration.

What you will do

  • Own the Platform roadmap and technical priorities, turning the needs of engineering teams and the business into clear objectives, supported by relevant metrics

  • Lead and support two Staff Engineers and one SRE, creating the environment, feedback, and team rituals they need to do their best work

  • Stay hands-on with backend and platform engineering, contributing to implementation, reviewing designs, and helping the team solve complex technical problems

  • Improve observability across the platform, bringing together metrics, logs, and traces with OpenTelemetry and meaningful SLIs and SLOs

  • Strengthen platform security and scalability, making sure our foundations support international growth and sharp traffic peaks

  • Improve developer experience across databases, CI/CD, service hosting, and repository management so teams can build and ship more effectively

  • Tackle technical debt and distributed architecture challenges, balancing immediate needs with the long-term health of the platform

  • Partner with engineering teams on the revamp of our end-user API, and help shape shared backend architecture principles and guidelines

  • Work closely with Engineering, Data, and Ops to build a platform that serves the whole company

The job is for you if

Must-have

  • You have 5**+ years of engineering experience**, including experience leading a backend or platform team as an Engineering Manager or Tech Lead in a startup that scaled

  • You have strong backend expertise, preferably in TypeScript / JavaScript, and want to remain hands-on for around 60% of your time

  • You have a deep understanding of PostgreSQL and solid knowledge of backend architecture patterns such as DDD

  • You have solid experience with AWS infrastructure, including services such as IAM, S3, EC2, EKS, and RDS

  • You know how to lead experienced engineers, providing clear direction, useful feedback, and autonomy

  • You can own a technical roadmap, define measurable objectives, and balance reliability, delivery speed, and business priorities with a pragmatic approach

  • You communicate clearly in French and English, and collaborate with humility, ownership, and proactivity

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with OpenTelemetry, SLIs, and SLOs

  • Experience improving developer tooling, CI/CD, and shared engineering workflows

  • Experience leading API refactoring or distributed architecture improvements

  • A passion for live music, entertainment, and the engineering challenges behind large ticket sales

jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Business Continuity & Crisis Management Officer will be responsible for developing, establishing, and implementing a comprehensive Business Continuity and Crisis Management Framework across the organization.

The role focuses on building business continuity processes, policies, and procedures from the ground up to strengthen organizational resilience, minimize operational disruptions, and ensure preparedness for potential crises.

The position will work closely with management and various business units to identify risks, assess business-critical functions, develop response and recovery strategies, and establish an effective enterprise-wide business continuity program.

Key Responsibilities

Business Continuity Planning & Development

  • Develop and implement an enterprise-wide Business Continuity Management (BCM) Framework from the ground up.
  • Establish business continuity policies, procedures, standards, and governance structures.
  • Conduct Business Impact Analysis (BIA) to identify critical functions, dependencies, and recovery priorities.
  • Develop Business Continuity Plans (BCPs) and recovery strategies for different departments and business units.
  • Identify potential threats and vulnerabilities that may affect organizational operations.

Crisis Management & Response

  • Establish a Crisis Management Framework, including escalation procedures, communication protocols, and incident response guidelines.
  • Develop crisis response strategies for operational disruptions, emergencies, natural disasters, and other business-critical incidents.
  • Define roles, responsibilities, and decision-making protocols during crisis situations.
  • Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to ensure preparedness and effective crisis response.

Risk Assessment & Organizational Resilience

  • Conduct enterprise-wide risk and continuity assessments.
  • Collaborate with department heads to identify operational risks and business dependencies.
  • Recommend mitigation measures and recovery strategies to minimize business interruptions.
  • Align continuity and crisis management initiatives with organizational objectives and recognized industry standards.

Implementation, Testing & Continuous Improvement

  • Facilitate the implementation of business continuity and crisis management procedures across business units.
  • Organize crisis simulations, tabletop exercises, and business continuity testing activities.
  • Evaluate organizational preparedness and identify areas for improvement.
  • Provide training and awareness sessions to employees and key stakeholders.
  • Maintain and periodically review continuity plans and crisis response procedures.

Governance & Stakeholder Coordination

  • Work closely with senior management and cross-functional teams to establish business continuity governance and accountability.
  • Prepare documentation, reports, recommendations, and progress updates.
  • Ensure business continuity practices are aligned with relevant regulations, organizational policies, and industry standards.
  • Support the long-term sustainability and continuous improvement of the organization's business continuity program.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Risk Management, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in Business Continuity Management, Crisis Management, Operational Resilience, Enterprise Risk Management, or related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated experience developing or implementing business continuity frameworks, policies, and procedures.
  • Experience conducting Business Impact Analysis, risk assessments, crisis preparedness planning, and continuity testing.
  • Familiarity with ISO 22301, business continuity management principles, and crisis management best practices.
  • Strong analytical, project management, documentation, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to coordinate with multiple business units and communicate effectively with senior leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background in diversified corporations, infrastructure, financial services, utilities, logistics, or other organizations with complex operations.
  • Hands-on experience establishing business continuity or crisis management programs from scratch.
  • Certifications such as Certified Business Continuity Professional (CBCP), Member of the Business Continuity Institute (MBCI), or ISO 22301 Lead Implementer are advantageous.

Key Competencies

  • Business Continuity Management (BCM)
  • Crisis Management & Incident Response
  • Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
  • Enterprise Risk Assessment
  • Business Continuity Planning (BCP)
  • Disaster Recovery & Recovery Planning
  • Operational Resilience
  • Crisis Communication & Escalation
  • Policy & Framework Development
  • Stakeholder Management
  • Business Continuity Testing & Simulation

jobs.excerpt: Overview We are seeking a senior leader with a proven record of bringing complex technical transformations to completion.
jobs.description:
Overview

We are seeking a senior leader with a proven record of bringing complex technical transformations to completion. This leader will own end-to-end execution, translating strategic objectives into an integrated delivery plan and establishing the discipline, transparency, and accountability required to achieve measurable business outcomes. The mandate is not simply to coordinate work or report progress; it is to drive decisions, resolve barriers, and deliver a successful transformation through implementation, adoption, stabilization, and operational handoff.

The successful candidate will combine technical fluency, operational rigor, and executive influence to align technology, product, operations, finance, and other business stakeholders around a single execution framework. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can bring structure to ambiguity, challenge unsupported assumptions, and maintain delivery momentum without compromising quality or business continuity.

Responsibilities

  • Own delivery through completion. Establish accountability for transformation scope, schedule, investment, quality, adoption, and business outcomes. Define what completion means and secure agreement on measurable acceptance criteria.
  • Build one integrated execution plan. Translate the transformation into sequenced workstreams, deliverables, milestones, critical-path dependencies, resource requirements, and named accountable owners. Reconcile technical delivery plans with operational readiness and business commitments
  • Install rigorous governance. Establish a consistent operating cadence for workstream reviews and executive decisions. Maintain a single source of truth for commitments, decisions, dependencies, and performance, and give the executive team and sponsors clear recommendations and timely decision requests.
  • Enforce stage-gate discipline. Apply the gate framework below. Surface unmet criteria explicitly and require documented decisions on remediation, exceptions, or changes before proceeding.
  • Drive technical execution. Partner with engineering, architecture, product, data, security, and infrastructure leaders to challenge estimates, validate sequencing, and resolve integration, migration, testing, scalability, and release-readiness issues.
  • Manage risks and recovery. Identify delivery threats early, quantify their implications, assign mitigation owners, and execute recovery plans. Escalate unresolved issues with clear options, trade-offs, recommendations, and decision deadlines.
  • Control scope and investment. Establish disciplined change control and assess requests against business value, capacity, cost, delivery timing, and risk. Make the consequences of reprioritization visible before commitments change.
  • Measure outcomes, not activity. Establish baselines, targets, metric definitions, data sources, and accountable owners. Use leading and lagging indicators to distinguish completed tasks from accepted deliverables and realized business value.
  • Lead cross-functional execution. Align teams and external partners around shared commitments and resolve competing priorities, promoting fact-based problem solving and timely escalation.
  • Cultivate high-performing teams. Build, mentor, and retain top-tier technical and program management talent, and create a team culture that applies best-in-class practices and sustains high customer satisfaction.
  • Lead with accountability and principle. Set clear goals and roles, hold leaders and teams to their commitments through candid feedback and prompt corrective action, and model integrity, transparency, and sound judgment.
  • Secure adoption and sustained results. Integrate process redesign, communications, training, support readiness, and operational controls into the delivery plan. Own stabilization and handoff to permanent operational owners, including benefits tracking and formal closure.

Milestones and Decision Gates

  • Establish a fit-for-purpose gate framework that connects technical progress to business readiness. Each gate needs an accountable owner, a committed date, objective acceptance criteria, supporting evidence, and a designated decision-maker. The framework should address:
  • Mobilization and baseline: Approved scope, business case, delivery plan, resourcing, dependencies, success measures, and governance.
  • Design and execution readiness: Validated requirements, solution approach, integration and data plans, operational impacts, and test strategy.
  • Release and deployment readiness: Evidence of testing, defect disposition, migration readiness, security and operational approvals, training, support coverage, and contingency plans.
  • Stabilization and operational acceptance: Demonstrated performance against agreed service and quality thresholds, resolved or formally accepted issues, and operational-owner sign-off.
  • Benefits validation and closure: Accepted deliverables, verified outcomes against the business case, assigned ownership for ongoing benefits, and completed transition documentation.

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed and is not to be construed as an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties and skills required. This job description does not constitute an employment agreement and is subject to change as the needs of Cotiviti and requirements of the job change.

Qualifications

  • 12+ years of progressive technology leadership, including 5+ years in executive roles and large-scale project delivery in global organizations.
  • Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred.
  • Demonstrated success designing transformation strategy and multi-year roadmaps at enterprise or global scale, and leading complex, cross-functional technical transformations through implementation, stabilization, and formal completion to measurable business Experience limited to strategy, advisory, or program reporting is not sufficient.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional technical transformations from planning through implementation, stabilization, and formal completion—not solely strategy development, advisory support, or program reporting.
  • A verifiable delivery record supported by specific examples of transformation scope, personal accountability, major obstacles resolved, delivery commitments achieved, and quantified business
  • Experience establishing disciplined execution frameworks with integrated plans, critical-path management, milestone tracking, stage gates, change control, and executive-level performance
  • Strong technical fluency across software delivery, systems integration, data migration, testing, and production operations, with the ability to challenge assumptions and engage credibly with technical leaders.
  • Proven ability to recover challenged initiatives, resolve interdependent issues, and drive timely decisions across organizational boundaries.
  • Strong financial and operational judgment, including experience managing budgets, resource constraints, delivery trade-offs, and benefits realization.
  • Ability to influence senior stakeholders, communicate difficult issues transparently, and hold teams and partners accountable for agreed commitments.
  • Senior-executive presence: influences senior stakeholders, presents to executive leadership teams and boards, communicates difficult issues transparently, and leads enterprise governance across business units and geographies.
  • Experience leading organizational readiness, adoption, and transition to sustainable operational ownership.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt certification, or equivalent demonstrated experience applying structured continuous improvement, root-cause analysis, process control, and data-driven problem solving.
  • Experience integrating Lean, Agile, and traditional program delivery methods into a practical governance model suited to the transformation.
  • Experience delivering enterprise platform modernization in complex, regulated, or operationally intensive environments. Healthcare experience is a plus.
  • Relevant program management, change management, or technical delivery credentials supported by a strong execution record.

Cognitive / Mental Requirements:

  • Strategic and systems thinking: Connects enterprise strategy to execution and anticipates how decisions affect technology, operations, and business outcomes.
  • Complex problem solving: Breaks down ambiguous, interdependent problems, finds root causes, and develops practical solutions.
  • Analytical and data-driven judgment: Interprets quantitative and qualitative information to challenge assumptions, spot trends, and make evidence-based decisions.
  • Decision-making under pressure: Weighs trade-offs, risk, and incomplete information to make timely, well-reasoned decisions.
  • Planning and prioritization: Sequences work, manages dependencies, and focuses resources on the highest-value priorities across multiple workstreams.
  • Learning agility: Quickly absorbs new technical, operational, and industry concepts and adapts as conditions change

Physical Requirements and Working Conditions:

  • Remaining in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods.
  • Repeating motions that may include the wrists, hands and/or fingers.
  • Required to travel up to (15%) per year, as needed
  • Must be able to provide a dedicated, secure work area.
  • Must be able to provide high-speed internet access / connectivity and office setup and maintenance.

Location: Remote, must reside in one of the following states: MA, CT, NY, NJ, PA, RI, DE, MD, NH, VT

This Wetland Scientist opportunity is for a flexible and self-motivated individual that is willing to learn and grow as part of a team while providing wetlands and permitting expertise to projects within the Sediment and Risk Assessment (SRA) and Remediation (REM) service lines at EHS Support. As a Wetland Scientist, you will be joining a high-performance team of risk assessors, toxicologists, ecologists, scientists, and engineers that is focused on providing high-quality technical and strategic solutions to a variety of clients. Your primary responsibilities in the Wetland Scientist position will include assisting EHS Support’s wetland and waterways capabilities, including wetlands assessment, delineation, permitting, and restoration services. You will also be responsible for engaging in technical writing for development and delivery of technical reports or other regulatory submittals at the federal, state, and local levels to report findings for routine and complex sites.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Support development of federal, state, and local regulatory permitting processes to obtain authorization for construction and environmental remediation activities that may impact wetlands, waterways, or other regulated natural resources.
  • Ability to travel to project locations throughout the U.S.
  • Perform surveys in outdoor environments that require carrying equipment through forested areas.
  • Lead assessment, delineation, and classification of wetlands, waterways, or other regulated natural resources.
  • Support efficient and compliant permitting paths, develop required permit applications, and assist in coordination with regulatory agencies through permit application approval.
  • Provide occasional technical support to projects focused on ecological risk assessment, sediment assessment and remediation, biodiversity and ecological services, Natural Resource Damage Assessment (NRDA), and water quality compliance.
  • Obtaining, organizing, reviewing, and synthesizing environmental data in an organized and concise manner.
  • Engaging in technical writing to report findings to support investigation objectives.
  • Supporting the preparation of high-quality technical deliverables, reports, and presentations.
  • Planning and conducting field investigations as a lead to collect hydrologic, hydric soil, hydrophytic vegetation, and stream assessment data in support of wetland and surface water delineation surveys.
  • Prepare technical reports and supporting documentation for jurisdictional determination requests and assist with the development of permit application packages for federal, state, and local regulatory agencies.
  • Documenting field observations and recording necessary data to support multi-media field programs.
  • Ensuring field work is conducted in accordance with relevant investigation work plans and in accordance with prescribed standard operating procedures (SOPs) and wetland delineation methodologies and reporting.
  • Communicating (both written and verbal) the findings of data analyses and interpretation to both lay and technical audiences.

Specific Experience and Skills

  • 1-3 years of experience in environmental consulting, with a focus in freshwater and coastal wetlands assessment and permitting (NJ, NY, and PA experience preferred).
  • Experienced in independently performing wetland and surface water delineations consistent with wetland delineation manual standards for Northcentral and Northeast Region, including field data collection, survey documentation, preparation of Wetland Determination Data Forms and Ordinary High Water Mark Field Identification Data Sheets, aquatic resource mapping, and wetland functional assessments.
  • Ability to support and implement field investigations in wetland and surface water delineations, wetland function and value assessment, habitat assessment, and technical writing experience with Section 404, Section 10, Section 401 WQC, and state wetland permitting programs.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail and data quality.
  • Proficiency or understanding of Geographic Information Systems (GIS), global positioning system (GPS) units (e.g., Trimble) and other field monitoring equipment (e.g., multi-parameter water quality monitors, data logging instrumentation).
  • Ability to develop and maintain positive relationships with clients and co-workers.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • An understanding of environmental regulations and guidance under state wetland programs, and Northcentral and Northeast Region federal programs (e.g., RCRA, CERCLA, and CWA).
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills.

Education and Licenses

  • Build observability for the exchange: metrics, logging, tracing, dashboards, and actionable alerting tied to SLOs for latency and availability.

About You

Moving at our pace brings a lot of change, complexity, and ambiguity—and a little bit of chaos. Shopifolk thrive on that and are comfortable being uncomfortable. That means Shopify is not the right place for everyone.
Before you apply, consider if you can:
  • Care deeply about what you do and about making commerce better for everyone

About the role

Data is a crucial part of Shopify’s mission to make commerce better for everyone. We organize and interpret petabytes of data to provide solutions for our merchants and stakeholders across the organization.
As a Data Engineer at Shopify, your primary responsibility will be to contribute to Shopify’s Data Warehouse. Your work will unlock powerful insights to guide the development and improvement of Shopify’s products.
As an embedded Data Engineer, you will work directly building foundations for products that transform merchants' lives. You'll collaborate with a multidisciplinary team of professionals that can include Product Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, Business Analysts, and Product Management. The data you shape will be used to power product analysis, dashboards, and reports. You will also contribute by performing product analysis and creating dashboards and reports yourself from time to time. Get excited about flexing these analysis and reporting muscles, while also evangelizing the values and excellence in the Data Engineering craft to your multidisciplinary peers in a fast moving environment with competing priorities.
Our product is designed to empower entrepreneurs. Consequently, the work you do will not only create value for our users but also contribute to global entrepreneurship. To thrive here, you need to be dedicated to your craft and committed to constant development. You should be an independent thinker who can solve complex problems and handle a bit of chaos without breaking a sweat.
Example day to day responsibilities include:
  • Working with business partners to understand business and product objectives and identify the data needed to support them
  • Designing, building, implementing, and documenting data models
  • Writing data transformations using dbt or Spark
  • Shipping data pipelines including real-time streaming and batch processing
  • Optimizing data transformation pipelines to increase freshness or reduce computational time/cost
  • Working with engineers to understand and influence how data is produced
  • Collaborating with other data engineers on tooling for automated tasks around consuming, validating raw/modeled data, updating modeled data
  • Subscribing to and implementing architecture and standards following the Data Engineer craft at Shopify
  • Collaborating with sister disciplines (Engineering, Data Science) to establish best practices and evangelize the values and priorities of the Data Engineering craft
  • Partnering closely with product, engineering and other business leaders to influence product and program decisions with data
  • Building production-quality dashboards and scalable data products

About The Role:

WebEngage’s Data Engineering team is the backbone of our analytics, personalisation, and machine-learning capabilities. As a Data Engineer, you will own the end-to-end lifecycle of data — from ingesting raw event streams and third-party feeds to building well-modelled, highly reliable datasets that power dashboards, predictive models, and customer journey orchestration. This is a high-impact, hands-on role where you will work at the intersection of product, analytics, and backend engineering. You will be expected to think beyond just moving data — designing for data quality, pipeline observability, cost efficiency, and long-term maintainability from day one.

Responsibilities:

Pipeline Development & Reliability

  • Design, build, and maintain production-grade ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest data from APIs, databases, event streams (Kafka/Pub-Sub), and flat files into the central data warehouse.
  • Implement idempotent, incremental load patterns with built-in retry logic, dead-letter queues, and SLA-based alerting to ensure zero-data-loss pipelines.
  • Own pipeline observability — set up data freshness checks, row-count validations, schema drift detection, and anomaly alerts using tools like Great Expectations or dbt tests.

Data Modelling & Warehouse Design

  • Translate business requirements into clean dimensional models (star/snowflake schemas) and maintain a well-documented data catalogue.
  • Design slowly changing dimensions (SCD Type 1/2), bridge tables, and fact tables optimised for analytical query patterns.
  • Enforce partitioning, clustering, and materialised view strategies to keep warehouse costs under control while maintaining sub-second query performance.

Code Quality & Engineering Best Practices

  • Write clean, modular, well-tested Python and SQL code. Follow DRY principles, use version control (Git), and participate in peer code reviews.
  • Build reusable transformation frameworks using dbt or equivalent tooling, with proper documentation and testing at every layer (staging → intermediate → mart).
  • Containerise data services with Docker and automate deployments via CI/CD pipelines (GitHub
Actions / GitLab CI).

BI, Visualization & Analytics

  • Build interactive dashboards and analytical tools using Streamlit, enabling stakeholders to explore metrics, run ad-hoc analyses, and make data-driven decisions without engineering dependency.
  • Design and maintain BI layers — semantic models, KPI definitions, and pre-aggregated mart tables that serve as the single source of truth for reporting across teams.
  • Translate raw data into compelling visual narratives using libraries like Plotly, Matplotlib, or Altair; present findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Partner with product managers, analysts, and data scientists to understand data needs and proactively identify gaps in current data coverage.
  • Document data lineage, transformation logic, SLAs, and known limitations in a shared knowledge base to enable self-service analytics.
  • Contribute to internal engineering guilds, knowledge-sharing sessions, and post-incident reviews for pipeline failures.

Requirements:

  • Strong SQL skills with expertise in complex queries, performance optimization, and cost-efficient design on cloud data warehouses (BigQuery, Redshift).
  • Strong Python scripting for data ingestion, transformation, and validation, with hands-on experience in Pandas, SQLAlchemy, APIs, and automation.
  • ETL/ELT- End-to-end ownership of data pipelines, including ingestion, transformation, and loading, with understanding of incremental loads, and backfills.
  • Data Modelling- Ability to design dimensional and transactional data models (star/snowflake, SCDs) and translate business needs into optimized table structures.

Good to Have:

  • Airflow, dbt, Docker, CI/CD
  • GCP/AWS, data warehousing concepts
  • BI tools / Streamlit / visualization

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related quantitative field (or equivalent practical experience).
  • 1–3 years of professional experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, or a backend role with significant data pipeline work.
  • Strong understanding of data warehouse architecture — know when to use wide denormalised tables vs. normalised models, and the trade-offs of each.
  • Familiarity with version control workflows (Git branching strategies, pull requests, code reviews) and agile development practices.
  • A data quality mindset — you instinctively validate assumptions, add assertions to pipelines, and treat silent data failures as critical incidents.

jobs.excerpt: Want to lead research projects for the world’s leading brands?
jobs.description:
Want to lead research projects for the world’s leading brands? How about rethinking the way brand’s commission and perform those projects in a leaner faster fashion?

Contently is hiring a Research Director capable of leading research projects to be leveraged as compelling articles, video, and infographics for our own publication The Content Strategist and clients titles. This is an extension of Contently’s ongoing mission to empower brands’ to reach their audiences through story.

The role will be a temporary part-time position, but we anticipate the hours and involvement to evolve and increase as we proceed.

What You’ll Do:

  • Project management: Acts as a team leader for corporate research projects, coordinating all aspects of complex research resources including subject matter experts, data analysts, designers, and editors.
  • Research generation: Participates in the conceptualization and writing of key research deliverables, including research briefs, survey profiles, and the final research report.
  • Data collection and gathering: Works with a wide variety of organizations and partners to administer research surveys and or/gather key marketing and research data using either existing or new data models.
  • Analyst work: Interacts directly with Contently clients and external parties (in-person, telephone) to gather and review research findings as well as discuss business-related problems/issues.
  • Segmentation & Profiling: Understand market analysis, customer segmentation, and content marketing strategies that help develop target audiences and customer personas for Contently clients’ market opportunities.
  • Service development: Works with our other research analysts to ensure on-time delivery of research results and reports to Contently client/s
  • Client-facing activities: Delivers on ad hoc consulting projects as needed (e.g. benchmarking, go-to-market, assessments) as well as research presentations (internal and external).

Who You Are:

  • Experience with consumer research including quantitative and qualitative survey development and analysis, as well as development of meaningful research conclusions and business implications, as well as deep consumer insights
  • Experience with marketing channels such as traditional TV, radio, print, display, search and mobile research metrics, platforms and tools such as Galaxy, nPower, Adviews, NTI, C3, ratings projections, ComScore, Ad relevance, MRI, Simmons, Scarborough, Arbitron, etc.
  • Customer-facing skills (strong presenter, comfortable with executive-level audience, able to identify issues/needs through effective questioning)
  • Experience creating reports and dashboards used to deliver insights in a format that is consumable/usable at multiple types of audiences. Familiarity with current tools for data models, and visualization across multiple and disparate data sources.
  • Experience with measurement plans, campaign testing, market mix modeling, ROI, in-market testing, and ad/media evaluation
  • Experience both in managing people and as a team player interacting with different functional areas and personality styles.
  • Demonstrated ability in forming trusted advisor relationships with internal partners or external clients.
  • A proven track record of triangulating disparate data and turning them into business recommendations and actions.
  • BA/BS in statistics, economics, or market research preferred; MBA or Masters degree a plus

More on Contently:

Contently is on a mission to change the way content marketing is traditionally done. That means not only building a powerful technology but also leveraging a powerful network of creative experts that traditional marketers need to stay fresh and original. Working at Contently means that you will be collaborating with extremely intelligent, creative, and diverse problem-solvers who love a good story and many laughs.

jobs.title: Database Administrator (Fully Remote)
jobs.excerpt: Description ﻿Who We Are - Motivated by Purpose.  Powered by Clinical Expertise.
jobs.description:
Description

﻿Who We Are - Motivated by Purpose. Powered by Clinical Expertise.

Founded in 1983, we’re a clinically-driven, tech-enabled utilization management company offering expert clinical reviews, regulatory guidance, and actionable insights to healthcare organizations.

Excellence starts with our people.

WE OFFER

  • A competitive compensation package
  • Benefits include healthcare, vision, and dental insurance
  • A generous 401(k) match
  • Paid vacation, PTO, and holidays
  • Growth and training opportunities
  • An award-winning remote work environment

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Database Administrator is responsible for the health, performance, security, and architecture of the organization's relational and NoSQL/document database platforms across on-premises and cloud environments. During a period of significant modernization, this role keeps on-premises SQL Server stable while leading the design and migration of transactional workloads to Azure and supporting the move to Microsoft Fabric. The position partners with Software Development, QA, Infrastructure, Enterprise Architecture, Information Security, Business Intelligence, and vendors, taking a prevention-first approach to protecting PHI and the organization's data.

Roles:

  • Primary technical owner and escalation point for all production and non-production databases and data stores, on-premises and in the cloud.
  • Lead database architecture, design standards, and Azure migration strategy in alignment with enterprise architecture.
  • Primary database partner to application development, QA, and Business Intelligence teams.
  • Proactively identify and resolve performance, capacity, security, and stability risks before they become incidents.

Major Responsibilities or Assigned Duties:

On-prem SQL Server Operations & Decommissioning

  • Administer, patch, secure, and support on-premises SQL Server (SQL Agent, SSIS, linked servers), keeping it stable through the transition.
  • Inventory databases, dependencies, and data flows to sequence migration; decommission servers once workloads move.

Azure Cloud Database Architecture & Migration

  • Lead design of the Azure transactional environment (Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, SQL on Azure VMs), including tiers, sizing, HA, networking, and security, through the architecture review process.
  • Oversee the on-prem to Azure migration from assessment through cutover, validation, and rollback; manage consumption and cost.

Multi-Platform Data Environment

  • Support database workloads hosted on various cloud platforms (e.g., Cloud SQL, BigQuery, PostgreSQL) with consistent standards.
  • Advise on the move to Microsoft Fabric, including source design, data movement, and integration with the Lakehouse and warehouse.

NoSQL and Document Platforms

  • Administer and support NoSQL and document databases (e.g., Azure Cosmos DB, MongoDB), including partition/shard key design, indexing policies, consistency levels, throughput and cost management, and backup/restore.
  • Partner with Development and Infrastructure on data integrity and consistency across relational and NoSQL/document databases, including idempotency and retry patterns.
  • Extend monitoring, alerting, PHI protection, auditing, and backup/DR standards to NoSQL and document databases.

Proactive Monitoring, Security & Continuity

  • Maintain monitoring, alerting, health checks, and performance baselines; tune queries and indexes and drive root cause analysis.
  • Configure auditing to Information Security's SIEM; design and test backup, HA, and DR to RPO/RTO targets; support audits (e.g., HIPAA, SOC 2, HITRUST, URAC).

Application Development, BI & QA Partnership

  • Partner with developers and BI on data modeling, schema design, and query patterns; review database code and changes before release.
  • Guide QA on database testing standards (integrity, regression, load, performance), with QA retaining ownership of test strategy.
  • Partner with QA on database acceptance criteria, masked test data, unit testing, and defect triage.
  • Manage database change control and deployments across environments under the IT change management process.

Standards & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish database standards, runbooks, and documentation; automate routine tasks; advise on licensing and emerging tools.

Other duties as assigned

Requirements

Skills:

  • Expert SQL Server administration and T-SQL, including performance tuning, indexing, andquery plan analysis.
  • Strong OLTP and analytical data modeling and database design.
  • Deep knowledge of Azure database services (security, networking, HA, cost); familiarity with Google Cloud data services.
  • Database security, encryption, and auditing, including PHI/HIPAA protection, Entra ID, Key Vault, and Defender for SQL.
  • Working knowledge of NoSQL/document databases (e.g., Cosmos DB, MongoDB), including data modeling, partitioning, and consistency.
  • Scripting (PowerShell, Python) and source control/CI/CD for database changes (Git, Azure DevOps, SSDT, Flyway).
  • Prevention-first mindset, strong documentation habits, and clear communication with technical and non-technical audiences.

Experience:

  • 5+ years as a SQL Server DBA supporting business-critical production systems.
  • 2+ years administering and designing databases in Microsoft Azure.
  • Led or played a key role in at least one database migration.
  • Production experience with at least one NoSQL/document database platform preferred.
  • Supporting development, QA, and BI teams within an Agile SDLC and formal change management.
  • Healthcare or regulated-environment experience strongly preferred; Microsoft Fabric experience strongly preferred.

Certifications (Preferred):

  • DP-300, AZ-305, Google Professional Cloud Database Engineer, DP-700/DP-600 (or
  • Snowflake/Databricks equivalent), Security+, or ITIL Foundation.

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent education and experience.

Work Environment:

Remote (work-from-home) position requiring standard computer and telephone use. On-call rotation and occasional after-hours or weekend work for maintenance, migrations, and incidents are required

Diversity Statement:

Diversity creates a healthier atmosphere: All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law.

﻿

Drug-Free Workplace:

This company is a drug-free workplace. All candidates are required to pass a Background Screen before beginning employment. All newly hired employees will take a Drug Screen, as well as agreeing to all necessary Compliance Regulations on their first day of employment. Employees are required to adhere to all applicable HIPAA regulations and company policies and procedures regarding the confidentiality, privacy, and security of sensitive health information.

  • Sensitive Personal Info: MRIoA may collect sensitive personal info such as real name, nickname or alias, postal address, telephone number, email address, Social Security number, signature, online identifier, Internet Protocol address, driver’s license number, or state identification card number, and passport number.

jobs.excerpt: About the Organization:Healthy oceans need healthy data systems, and healthy information ecosystems need stewardship.
jobs.description:
About the Organization:Healthy oceans need healthy data systems, and healthy information ecosystems need stewardship. Intertidal Agency empowers ocean data stewards and helps build data infrastructure to drive ocean conservation, management, and innovation. We support the people layer of data sharing with a combination of policy, process, and technical tools. Our multi-disciplinary partners include governments, communities, scientists, nonprofits, and businesses who want to connect ocean data to action by making data more useful, usable, and used.
Position Summary:Intertidal Agency is seeking a data scientist or data engineer for a one-year fellowship to improve data pipelines into the World Ocean Database (WOD), the primary global source for ocean temperature, salinity, oxygen, and nutrient data. The overall project goal is to make WOD data more FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) by standardizing workflows for data ingestion across a global community of data contributors. A specific focus for the fellow will be developing algorithmic solutions for de-duplicating data submissions from uncrewed systems, such as gliders, and expanding those solutions to address other ocean and earth science problems. Addressing this problem will require contending with three intersecting issues:
  • Identification. How do you determine that two records describe the same observation? The obvious matching key for glider data is unreliable, and finding better ones is part of the work.
  • Survivorship. Once duplicates are identified, which copy survives, and on what basis? Later submissions are often better, but not always. The rule must be defensible and documented.
  • Granularity. A glider may report every second. WOD cannot absorb that resolution across a growing fleet, and binning decisions determine what future researchers can ask of the record. Setting a community standard for granularity takes both analysis and community agreement.
Developing and publishing rigorous, community-supported solutions to these issues will be a significant contribution to WOD and the broader earth science field.
This is a one-year, fixed-term position that is supported by a Climate Reserve fellowship, and the hire will also participate in Climate Reserve network activities.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Establish and help manage a project advisory committee ocean data professionals.
  • Work directly with the major glider data providers (e.g. IOOS, EGO, and IMOS) on upstream improvements to data submissions.
  • Develop, test, and document an algorithmic method for identifying duplicate observations from gliders and other autonomous platforms, and for selecting which record to retain. Benchmark against the publicly served California Underwater Glider Network Line 80 record, roughly 67,000 quality-controlled profiles spanning 2005 to the present, then work against NOAA NCEI’s glider holdings.
  • Convene and run working sessions, including hackathons, to collaboratively develop solutions. Participants would include people experienced with the data sources, research software engineers, data scientists, and WOD experts. Support workshop participants in implementing and iterating on workshop products within their own workflows.
  • Release all code, computational notebooks, and documentation publicly under open licenses, written so that other data centers can adopt the methods. Prepare a manuscript for a peer-reviewed journal with the fellow as lead author.
  • Work with project directors and the advisory committee to draft recommendations for the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC) to support the new standards and workflows. These would be drafted during the fellowship and presented at the fall 2028 IOC meeting.

The Ideal Candidate

You are drawn to challenges that span disciplines. You can take a messy, real-world data problem and find structure in it. You write code other people can run and read. You work well with people with a wide range of technical fluency, from research software engineers to program managers and scientists. You have experience modernizing legacy data systems. You develop clear roadmaps and roles with your teammates that let you work independently while staying coordinated. You see AI as a tool to support human expertise and judgement, not a replacement.
You do not need to be an oceanographer. If you bring strong quantitative and data science skills, the project leads and advisors will provide the ocean science grounding.

Specific Experience Requested:We recognize that each applicant for this role will bring unique skills, knowledge, experiences, and background to this position. We welcome diverse experiences and perspectives in our applicant pool, and will be looking for candidates who possess many, but not necessarily all, of the following qualifications and experience:
  • Quantitative and algorithmic capability. Multivariate statistics and dimensionality reduction, similarity and distance metrics, clustering or classification. Experience with record linkage, entity resolution, fuzzy matching, or deduplication in any domain, including outside Earth science (e.g. bibliographic records, customer data, other sensor networks).
  • Working knowledge of why pairwise comparison across millions of records is not viable, and familiarity with blocking, indexing, approximate nearest neighbor search, or locality-sensitive hashing as ways around it.
  • Python fluency, preferably with numpy, pandas, and scipy. Version control with git.
  • Comfortable in a Unix or Linux shell on a remote machine, with pipes, regular expressions, and standard text processing tools. You will need to open an unfamiliar file, inspect it, and write something to interrogate it, with nobody available to walk you through it.
  • Reading and writing netCDF, including CF conventions, standard names, fill values, and time units. The majority of the data under consideration will be in this format. Familiarity with CF discrete sampling geometries, particularly Profile and TrajectoryProfile, is a strong plus, since that is how glider deployments are represented.
  • Retrieving data programmatically from ERDDAP, THREDDS, or OPeNDAP endpoints, and from federal repositories, university archives, and cloud object storage.
  • Independence. The ability to take an ambiguous problem, break it apart, and make progress without close supervision.
  • Experience handling data you did not collect, from providers you do not control, in formats you did not choose
  • Experience with government data infrastructure and modernizing legacy data systems
  • International research or data collaboration
  • Familiarity with oceanographic or earth science data

Workplace & Compensation

Workplace: Intertidal Agency has a fully remote workforce with a 32 hour work week. The fellow will be expected to be available during a core set of working hours (generally 0900-1300 Pacific Time) with some availability during UTC/Europe time.
Travel: Estimated three weeks of travel for two project workshops plus the annual Climate Reserve convening.
Compensation: Intertidal Agency and Multiplier provide a comprehensive compensation package, including competitive salary ($78k-$88k annual salary), excellent medical and dental benefits, retirement savings, and generous vacation and sick leave policy.

How to Apply: To apply, please visit our Applicant Portal. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. Priority will be given to applications received on or before Sunday, November 29, 2026. Please include your resume and a cover letter explaining your interest in the role. We respectfully request no follow-up calls or emails.

Intertidal Agency is an independent operating project ofMultiplier, a nationally recognized nonprofit that accelerates impact for sustainability-focused initiatives.
Multiplier is committed to creating an inclusive, equitable, and accessible application process for all candidates. We recognize that the traditional hiring process can create barriers. If we can support your participation in the job application or interview process by providing specific assistance or accommodation, please reach out to . Requests for accommodations are confidential and will not impact your candidacy.

jobs.title: Claims Performance Analyst
jobs.excerpt: About Reserv Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims.
jobs.description:
About Reserv

Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims. Founded by insurtech veterans with deep experience in SaaS and digital claims, Reserv is venture-backed by Bain Capital and Altai Ventures and began operations in May 2022. We are focused on automating highly manual tasks to tackle long-standing problems in claims and set a new standard for TPAs, insurance technology providers, and adjusters alike. We have ambitious (but attainable!) goals and need people who can work in an evolving environment. If building a leading TPA and the prospect of tackling the long-standing challenges of the claims role sounds exciting, we can't wait to meet you.

Location Requirement

Candidates must reside in an eligible U.S. state throughout employment. We are unable to hire candidates residing in California, Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, or outside the United States.

About the role

Reserv’s book is growing fast — and fast growth stress-tests everything: file quality, reserving discipline, assignment logic, and the processes underneath them. We’re standing up a small rapid-response function inside Claims Performance to get ahead of it, and we’re staffing it with four of our own.

  • Deployments will range across the full complexity spectrum of the book — from high-complexity GL and liability files to high-frequency APD inventory. The common thread isn’t the line of business; it’s a book under pressure that needs senior claims hands in it now.
  • You’re a licensed, tenured adjuster who will embed inside a claims team under pressure, dig into the inventory, and take direct corrective action in files — because you hold the licenses to do it. You diagnose like an auditor and operate like an adjuster.
  • You will also act as a requirements pipeline for embedding quality and compliance controls directly into our platform: every problem you find, fix, or coach to gets written up as a spec for an embedded check in Glance. Put plainly: your job is to work yourself out of a job. When the book stabilizes and the platform checks ship, you haven’t made yourself obsolete — you’ve made the fix permanent.

**This is a 6-12 month rotational tour, not a permanent position — and the same is true of the function itself. This program exists to close the gap while quality and compliance controls are built into Glance; as those embedded checks ship, the need for manual intervention shrinks, and the program sunsets with it. That’s not a risk to the role — it’s the definition of success. At the end of your tour you return to a guaranteed equivalent-or-better seat, carrying skills and visibility very few adjusters get.

You’ll sit on the Claims Performance team. The VP of Claims Performance and claims leadership point you at the book, set the priorities, and re-aim you as conditions change — you bring the file-level judgment on how to get there. Before your first deployment, the QA team will train you on Reserv’s AI-assisted review tooling — MAG (multi-agent review), Batch, and Copilot — so you’re diagnosing with machine leverage, not just a legal pad.

What you'll do

  • Embed in an assigned book of business. Review the claim inventory end to end and surface what’s actually wrong: aged and stalled files, miss-assigned claims, under-reserved exposures, and authority breaches.
  • Fix what you find. Where licensed and authorized, take corrective action in the file: documentation, reserve recommendations, reassignment flags, and escalation. You don’t write a finding and walk away; you leave the file better than you found it.
  • Shape the action plan, then work the clean-up through Claim Health. Provide direct input into claim action plans, then use Claim Health to drive the clean-up: prioritize the inventory, work it down, and verify the improvement is real. A known failure mode is files being “moved” without actually advancing — you’ll distinguish genuine file progression from superficial touches, and call out the difference.
  • Route what you can’t fix to the leader who can. Some findings belong to a desk, not a file — training gaps, assignment logic, authority practices. Those get documented and handed to the accountable claims leader through Claims Performance, and you track whether they’re actioned. You illuminate; line leadership enforces.
  • Provide direct coaching and feedback to adjusting staff. Every corrected file is a coaching opportunity. Deliver specific, file-grounded feedback to the adjusters behind the inventory — directly, constructively, and in the moment. The goal isn’t just a cleaner file; it’s a desk that doesn’t produce the problem again.
  • Turn every fix into a platform check. Each problem you correct by hand gets written up as a structured requirement/spec for an automated control in Glance, so the platform catches it next time and no human has to. Rinse, repeat, scale.
  • Be the technical claims brain for claims leadership. As leadership pressure-tests processes across the book, you supply the file-level expertise: what’s really happening in the inventory, and why.
  • Keep the lines clean with QA. You are first-line: you work files and you fix them. The independent QA team trains you, audits behind you, and picks up the audit-worthy patterns you hand off. You never audit your own work — that separation is what lets your file actions stand up to carrier and regulator scrutiny.

What You Bring

  • Senior adjuster experience with genuine range. GL/liability complexity is mandatory — that depth transfers to everything else — but you’re equally willing to grind through a high-frequency APD inventory. Deployments will demand both.
  • A completed licensing footprint. You’ve finished the licensing process and are maximally licensed — this role starts deployed, not in a licensing queue. You’ll maintain the footprint with company-supported CE.
  • Airtight file documentation discipline. Your corrective actions live in files that regulators, carriers, and QA will read.
  • Comfort with AI-assisted claims tooling — or strong aptitude and appetite to learn it. You’ll be trained on MAG, Batch, and Copilot before deployment.
  • Comfort operating in a directed, high-tempo model. Claims leadership sets the target and re-aims you as the book demands; you own how the work gets done in the file. If you need six months of runway on one desk, this isn’t your role.
  • The rare temperament this role demands: the diagnostic mindset of an auditor, the willingness to get your hands dirty in files, and the credibility to coach peers directly — including delivering feedback the recipient may not want to hear.
  • A sense of urgency — at all times. (That does not mean working at all hours.)

Why This Role

Visibility. You’ll work directly with the VP of Claims Performance and senior claims leadership, on the problems they care most about, with your findings shaping how they run the book.

Leverage. Fixing one file helps one claim. Writing the spec that becomes a Glance platform check helps every claim, forever. Very few adjuster roles let you build the system instead of just working inside it.

Trajectory. Your job is to work yourself out of a job — and so is the program’s. Rotation alumni return to the book as the adjusters who know the AI tooling, think in platform checks, and have run point for senior claims leadership. As this function sunsets, that experience is what you keep — and it’s the profile we expect to draw on for what comes next.

Working hours are aligned to claims leadership (US hours).

Benefits

  • Generous health-insurance package with nationwide coverage, vision, & dental
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching
  • Competitive PTO policy – we want our employees fresh, healthy, happy, and energized!
  • Generous family leave policy after 8 months of continuous work
  • 100% remote (home-based) role designed to support your work-life balance
  • Apple laptop, large second monitor, and other quality-of-life equipment you may want. Technology is something that should make your life easier, not harder!

At Reserv, we value diversity in backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences and believe that diversity in viewpoints and critical thinking drives innovation, first-principles thinking, and success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage those from all walks of life to apply. If you believe you are a good fit for this role, we would love to hear from you!

Working with the CEO, CMO, SMEs across the company, and agencies, you will also help shape the angles and messages behind them. Overview

KFS, LLC is seeking a Part-Time National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) Subject Matter Expert (SME) who will support environmental compliance and planning efforts. The Part-Time NEPA SME will provide senior-level technical expertise and guidance to staff- and project-level environmental specialists developing Environmental Assessments, Environmental Impact Statements, and other environmental planning and compliance documents. This person will serve as a technical authority for an environmental program supporting numerous Department of Defense services with environmental compliance and NEPA projects.

Job duties include, but are not limited to:

  • Provide senior-level environmental reviews, project scope and alternative development, field investigation support, planning, cost estimating, problem and conflict resolution, and scheduling guidance.
  • Conduct environmental troubleshooting and consultations, providing expert technical and project advice and guidance to clients, project managers, and interdisciplinary teams.
  • Conduct comprehensive technical and quality-control reviews of professional studies, reports, environmental analyses, and NEPA documents.
  • Collaborate with managers, environmental specialists, engineers and architects, legal staff, contract specialists, contractor personnel, and agency representatives to provide advice and insight regarding the resolution of unique and/or complex environmental compliance issues.
  • Provide technical reviews and review comments for Environmental Assessments, Environmental Impact Statements, Records of Environmental Consideration, Findings of No Significant Impact, Records of Decision, and supporting environmental studies and reports.
  • Prepare and review environmental scopes of work and provide technical support for responses to requests for proposals for environmental projects.
  • Provide expert in-house assessments of project impacts, best management practices, typical and creative mitigation measures, and the required studies, consultations, coordination, permitting requirements, costs, and timelines necessary for final project implementation.
  • Evaluate proposed actions and alternatives for compliance with NEPA and other applicable federal, state, and local environmental laws, regulations, executive orders, and Department of Defense policies.

jobs.title: Account Executive, Community
jobs.excerpt: A Note On How To Reach Us We're truly grateful that so many people have Foundant on their radar — it means a lot that our work resonates with others.
jobs.description:
A Note On How To Reach Us

We're truly grateful that so many people have Foundant on their radar — it means a lot that our work resonates with others. That said, due to the high volume of direct messages and emails we receive, cold outreach isn't the preferred way to be considered for a role, and we're not able to prioritize applications submitted this way. To apply for open positions, please visit our careers page, which is the fastest and most effective route to being considered.

About Foundant

At Foundant, we build mission-critical software for the social good ecosystem — helping foundations, grantmakers, nonprofits, and community organizations streamline their work, strengthen relationships, and maximize their impact. We serve the giving community worldwide with a comprehensive suite of solutions spanning grant management, community foundation software, and giving analytics.

We're a unified company shaped by strong roots across our product portfolio, and we operate with intention and purpose. Our team of ~350 people across six countries is connected by a shared North Star: to be the trusted partner and strategic advisor to the communities we serve.

Where You’ll Work:
  • As a remote-first workplace, we believe in offering flexibility and the freedom to work where it suits you best, while staying connected through technology. Our global network of talent is supported by physical office hubs and virtual collaboration, fostering a dynamic environment where innovation and growth thrive.
  • With office locations in Bozeman, MT, Toronto, Canada, and Dublin, Ireland, you'll be part of a globally connected team. Whether you're working remotely or from one of our office locations, you'll be contributing to a vibrant, collaborative culture focused on driving meaningful impact across the world.
WhatYou’llDo:
  • You’ll build your own pipeline. Consistent, personalized outreach to community foundations, higher education institutions, and other community-focused organizations is the foundation of your results. You see it as the best way to sharpen your craft, because earning a response to a cold email or call is the hardest part of selling. Marketing and BDR-sourced leads are a welcome bonus on top of your own efforts, never a substitute for them.
  • You’ll own the full sales cycle and its results, carrying each opportunity from first conversation through a signed deal.
  • You’ll run discovery that goes past the surface request, listening for the mission, constraints, and outcomes each organization is working toward, reading both the people and the process, and shaping solutions that fit what they’re trying to achieve.
  • You’ll deliver clear, compelling demos and proposals that connect Foundant’s solutions, from CommunitySuite for fund accounting and donor management to our grantmaking solutions and purpose-built AI, to the results your prospect cares about.
  • You’ll work through multi-stakeholder buying processes, including board and committee reviews, finance and accounting stakeholders, and security reviews, keeping every stakeholder informed and bringing in your director and senior colleagues as deals grow more complex.
  • You’ll think critically about how to position Foundant for each buyer and learn how our internal teams work together, so you know who to involve, when, and why.
  • You’ll use AI to work smarter, from account research to outreach to proposal preparation, and you’ll apply critical thinking to how you use it: checking its outputs, protecting data, and keeping your own judgment in the lead.
  • You’ll partner with Marketing, Revenue Operations, Product, and Client teams, and hand off every new client with full context so the team that takes over is set up to succeed from day one.
  • You’ll learn from senior Account Executives and your director, asking for feedback on discovery, demos, and deal strategy and applying it in your next conversation.
  • You’ll share what you’re hearing from buyers with your director and cross-functional partners, so what you learn in the field helps shape how we sell.
  • You’ll hold yourself accountable for accurate pipeline data and forecasts in our CRM, using that data to prioritize your time and flag risks early, including your own.
  • Other duties as assigned.
WhatYou’llNeed:
  • 2–5 years of B2B SaaS sales experience
  • Demonstrated history of meeting or exceeding sales targets in a full-cycle sales role
  • Experience building your own pipeline through proactive, personalized outbound outreach
  • Experience working multi-stakeholder sales cycles, ideally including procurement, board, committee, or security reviews
  • Sound judgment and critical thinking, including the ability to use AI tools thoughtfully and evaluate their output
  • Proficiency with a CRM platform for pipeline management and forecasting
  • Must be legally eligible to work in the United States
  • Great to have: Experience working at a community foundation or in the broader social good sector
  • Great to have: Accounting background or experience with accounting software, such as an ERP or fund accounting system
WhatYou’llBring to our Team Dynamics:

Adaptive Achievement

Owns a pipeline and a number, building that pipeline through self-driven outreach and keeping deals moving through shifting buyer priorities and long, multi-stakeholder buying cycles. Follows through when a deal gets hard, not just when it’s going well, and takes responsibility for outcomes, including misses.

Productive Collaboration

Works hand in hand with Marketing, Revenue Operations, Product, and Client teams, applying emotional intelligence to build trust across the organization. Hands off new clients with context, so the relationship doesn’t restart at signature.

Service Orientation

Job Title: Director, Market Access, Reimbursement & Patient Services Learning and

Biogen is seeking an experienced learning and development leader to direct capability development for Market Access, Reimbursement, Patient Access, and Patient Services teams across the North America commercial organization. Reporting to the Head of Commercial Learning & Development, this remote Director partners with senior leaders to translate business priorities into integrated learning strategies, leads a team responsible for execution, and ensures solutions build critical capabilities and deliver measurable business impact.
