jobs.description:
Title: Regional Finance Coordinator

Type of contract: Employment

Contract duration: 24-month fixed-term contract with possibleextension

Work time: Full-time position (40 hours per week)

Reporting to: Head of Programme Finance

Location: Home-based (ideally within GMT-6 and GMT time zone), with regular travel within the assigned portfolio

Start date: February 2027

Application deadline: 08/12/2026

Background

The Global Survivors Fund (GSF) was launched in October 2019 by Dr Denis Mukwege and Nadia Murad, 2018 Nobel Peace Prize laureates. Its mission is to enhance access to reparations for survivors of conflict-related sexual violence around the globe, thus responding to a gap long identified by survivors. GSF acts to provide interim reparative measures in situations where states or other parties are unable or unwilling to meet their responsibilities. GSF advocates for duty bearers as well as the international community to develop reparations programmes. It also guides states and civil society by providing expertise and technical support in designing reparations programmes. GSF’s survivor-centric approach is the cornerstone of its work.

Role Summary

The Regional Finance Coordinator is the senior finance partner for an assigned portfolio of countries, projects and grants to implementing partners. The role combines business partnering, donor financial management, partner-finance oversight, financial risk management and supporting sound financial management of partnerships.

Working closely with Regional, Country and Finance teams, the role maintains senior finance leadership and operational understanding through regular engagement and programme visits.

Position Responsibilities

Programme, Partner and Portfolio Finance

  • Act as senior Finance Business Partner to Regional and Country Teams, providing financial analysis, advice and constructive challenge to support programme design, planning, resource allocation and decision-making;

  • Lead the technical budgeting, forecasting and financial monitoring processes, based on input from Programme teams;

  • Maintain a consolidated portfolio view and produce relevant analysis, forecasts, KPIs and scenarios, communicating material risks and ensuring agreed actions are monitored;

  • Provide financial leadership throughout programme and partnership cycles, from design and partner selection through implementation, monitoring and closure;

  • Lead financial part of partner’s selection and partnership building, assessments, agree proportionate mitigation and strengthening plans, and advise programme and partnership decisions;

  • Oversee partner planning, forecasting, reporting and disbursement recommendations, ensuring financial information is satisfactory;

  • Ensure appropriate use of GSF funds through proportionate partner review, monitoring, controls, audit and escalate to Head of Programme Finance when required;

  • Provide contextualised training and technical guidance and apply GSF partner-finance tools and minimum standards proportionately to partner maturity, context and capacity;

  • Maintain operational understanding through regular engagement with Programme Teams, partners and programme visits.

Project-specific Funding Accountability

  • Lead development and quality review of project-specific donor budgets, aligned with programme design, donor rules, cost recovery and delivery capacity;

  • Ensure appropriate grant set-up, coding, allocation, monitoring and documentation in coordination with the relevant finance function;

  • Lead or quality-assure donor financial reports, budget revisions and financial input to grant amendments, ensuring accuracy, timeliness and consistency with programme progress;

  • Oversee cost-eligibility reviews, donor audits and expenditure verifications, ensuring complete responses and follow-up;

  • Monitor grant compliance, co-financing, foreign-exchange, cost-recovery and financial risks, escalating material issues.

Financial Risk, Controls and Assurance

  • Maintain programme and partner financial risk assessments and ensure proportionate controls, mitigation, assurance and escalation;

  • Exercise delegated controls and approvals in line with GSF policies, donor requirements and authority limits;

  • Plan partner financial reviews and risk-based audits, follow up on priority actions, and contribute with portfolio insight to organisation-wide assurance processes;

  • Identify and escalate material errors, suspected misuse, fraud indicators, control failures and other material concerns.

Functional Leadership and Continuous Improvement

  • Contribute to practical finance and partner-finance policies, systems, tools and guidance, promoting reliable data, simplified processes and shared learning;

  • Coordinate detailed country, grant and partner-finance activities with the Programme Finance Officer where available, providing technical direction and review while retaining portfolio-level financial accountability;

  • Provide technical leadership, coaching and quality assurance to colleagues supporting the portfolio, and contribute to cross-functional planning and support across portfolios.

Position Requirements

Education and Experience

  • Relevant professional finance or accounting qualification, advanced degree in finance, accounting, business administration or a related field, or equivalent substantial professional experience;

  • 10+ years of experience in programme finance, grant or partner-finance in an international, multi-country and multicurrency organisation operating in complex or humanitarian contexts;

  • Demonstrated experience of financial business partnering, budgeting, forecasting, donor financial management, partner due diligence, reporting, financial risk assessment and audit;

  • Experience strengthening local or national partners and applying proportionate approaches across different levels of financial maturity and capacity;

  • Strong knowledge of financial controls, donor compliance, cost eligibility and grant-management requirements;

  • Experience working across projects, country, regional and global levels.

Other Requirements

  • Excellent written and spoken English and Spanish; French and/or Arabic would be an asset;

  • Strong analytical judgement and ability to translate complex information into practical recommendations;

  • Ability to combine constructive challenge with partnership, coaching and contextual sensitivity;

  • High integrity, accountability and ability to identify and escalate material concerns;

  • Advanced spreadsheet skills and proficiency using financial, grant-management and reporting systems; Power BI experience is an asset;

  • Ability and willingness to travel regularly, including to complex environments;

  • Commitment to GSF’s survivor-centred values, safeguarding, inclusion and responsible stewardship.

How to Apply

Please click apply to submit your application including two references by 8th December 2026 (midnight CET).

Kindly note only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

The Global Survivors Fund (GSF) is dedicated to fostering diversity, gender balance, and inclusion, reflecting the varied landscapes where we operate and the communities we work with. We welcome applications from qualified professionals of all backgrounds, cultures, and beliefs. We particularly encourage candidates from regions where GSF is active to apply.

At GSF, we are committed to enforcing stringent Safeguarding policies, covering protection from exploitation, abuse, harassment, misuse of power, and discrimination, as well as child safeguarding and financial and fiscal integrity. We uphold a zero-tolerance approach to any form of unacceptable behaviour.

As part of our recruitment process, shortlisted candidates will be required to provide references from previous employers and complete a self-declaration.

GSF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, or hiring processes (i.e. application stage, interview stage, validation stage, appointment, or training). GSF will never request applicants’ bank account information.

Please note that candidates must be authorised to work in the country where the position is based at the time of application.

Your Data - If you choose to apply for this position, you will be providing us with your personal data, which will be processed solely for the purpose of selecting a candidate for this position. We will retain the personal data you share with us as part of the application process for six months from the application deadline, after which it will be deleted. Your personal data will be accessed only by our HR Staff managing the recruitment process and members of the selection panel. You have the right to a) request access to your personal data and information about how we process it, b) ask us to rectify any inaccurate personal data we hold about you c) request the deletion of your personal data or restrict its processing, and d) object to how we process your personal data. To exercise these rights, please contact . If you have any concerns or complaints about how GSF processes your personal data, please submit them to .

jobs.description:
Director, AI Product Management

Remote Opportunity

About Reveleer

Reveleer delivers a unified platform spanning risk adjustment, quality improvement, clinical intelligence, and member management for health plans and provider organizations navigating the complexity of value-based care. Trusted by 80+ customer organizations nationwide, the platform integrates data, analytics, and intelligent workflow automation into one governed system designed to support traceable documentation across diagnoses, quality measures, and submissions. With regulatory expertise and transparent, human-in-the-loop AI at its core, Reveleer supports organizations working to advance care quality, strengthen documentation integrity, and sustain the operational readiness needed to navigate audits with confidence.

Role Summary

The Product Director, AI defines and executes Reveleer’s AI product strategy across Risk Adjustment, Quality, Retrieval, and the broader platform. You own a portfolio of AI capabilities from discovery through development, launch, adoption, and commercialization. The job is to turn clinical, operational, and customer opportunities into AI products that scale and deliver measurable value.

This is an AI-native product role. Product management has moved away from day-to-day execution and toward strategy, human alignment, and rapid prototyping. You frame the problem, design intelligent systems and agent workflows, evaluate model performance against business goals, and decide when a system needs more learning, more guardrails, or a change of direction. You use AI tools in your own work every day, and you expect your team to do the same.

You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Data Science, Clinical Operations, Legal/Compliance, Security, and Go-to-Market teams, and directly with customers. Together you make sure every AI release meets enterprise standards for accuracy, transparency, security, and responsible adoption.

Current Portfolio

Day one ownership includes the following. Scope will expand as Reveleer’s AI services converge on a shared platform.

What you own

GenECS-Generative AI for evidence capture and coding support; expansion, adoption strategy, and CSM enablement.

Skyline-Next-generation AI product roadmap, including release strategy for generative AI under customer and contractual constraints.

Retrieval / agentic AI-Agentic workflows that automate and accelerate medical record retrieval.

Smart Overread-ML-prioritized quality review that targets the charts most likely to contain errors while preserving objective accuracy reporting.

AI benchmarking-Reveleer’s Value-Based Care AI Benchmark and the evaluation methods behind it.

Emerging AI-New AI services and agents, prioritized against reuse across the platform.

Key Responsibilities

AI Product Strategy & Portfolio

  • Define and maintain the AI product strategy, portfolio priorities, and roadmap.
  • Find high-value opportunities to apply generative AI, machine learning, agentic workflows, and automation across Reveleer products.
  • Recommend investments and priorities based on customer value, operational impact, unit economics, technical feasibility, differentiation, and commercial potential.
  • Favor reusable AI services over one-off features so each initiative strengthens the broader platform.
  • Help score and prioritize candidate AI agents on value, economics, reusability, readiness, and risk.

AI-Native Discovery & Prototyping

  • Use AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Figma Make to speed up competitive research, synthesize customer and user feedback, and build working prototypes to test with users before committing to full development.
  • Run market and competitive analysis specific to payer, provider, and value-based care workflows.
  • Set the standard for AI-assisted product work on the team, and keep experimenting with new tools that shorten the development cycle.

Product Definition & Execution

  • Own AI products through discovery, requirements, definition, development, validation, release, and ongoing optimization.
  • Write clear product definition documents covering the problem, personas, workflows, scope, ML approach, operational workflow, acceptance criteria, and quantitative success metrics. These should be easy for AI, Data, Engineering, and Marketing teams to act on asynchronously.
  • Design intelligent workflows rather than standalone UIs: orchestrate AI agents, set human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and integrate models with internal and external APIs.
  • Work with Data Science and Engineering on model and product architecture, confidence thresholds, and integration into production workflows.
  • Define rollout strategies and adoption plans, including moving customers and users from legacy workflows to AI-enabled experiences.

AI Evaluation & Quality

  • Design evaluation frameworks that measure model outputs against business, clinical, and user goals. Contribute to Reveleer’s AI benchmarking program.
  • Be accountable for failure modes, bias, drift, and reliability in production, and decide when to add guardrails, retrain, or change direction.
  • Track both product metrics (adoption, retention, productivity, ROI) and AI metrics (precision, recall, confidence, latency, and cost per transaction).

AI Governance & Responsible Deployment

  • Work with Legal, Compliance, Security, Engineering, and leadership to set release and governance approaches for AI capabilities.
  • Spot contractual, regulatory (HIPAA, NCQA, CMS), privacy, security, and customer-policy constraints on generative AI early, and design alternative release paths when they apply.
  • Define controls such as customer gating, consent, human review, monitoring, and model-performance measurement.
  • Turn technical AI considerations into clear product decisions.

Commercialization & Customer Adoption

  • Build positioning and value propositions that turn complex AI capabilities into clear customer benefits.
  • Work with Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Clinical teams on launch readiness, pricing and packaging input, and enablement.
  • Build customer trust, readiness, policy, and contract considerations into rollout and adoption plans.
  • Represent Reveleer’s AI products with customers, advisory boards, and industry forums.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Connect Product, Engineering, Data Science, Clinical, Operations, Legal/Compliance, and GTM on AI.
  • Drive product decisions where clinical workflows, machine intelligence, operations, and customer requirements meet.
  • Explain direction, trade-offs, risks, progress, and business outcomes clearly to leadership, customers, and non-technical teams.
  • Lead product direction for shared AI capabilities that span multiple product lines, and share AI-native practices with fellow PMs.

Qualifications

Required

  • 7+ years of product management experience, including experience owning complex products or major platform capabilities.
  • A track record of taking AI/ML products from concept through production and commercialization.
  • Technical fluency in generative AI, LLM-enabled applications, RAG, fine-tuning, agentic workflows, model evaluation, and human-in-the-loop design, plus enough depth in APIs and data pipelines to hold credible conversations with engineering teams.
  • Hands-on, daily use of AI tools for research, synthesis, prototyping, and product definition.
  • Sound judgment when outcomes are uncertain and models are non-deterministic, balancing innovation, customer value, regulatory requirements, technical feasibility, and speed to market.
  • Experience working directly with Engineering and Data Science teams.
  • The ability to explain complex AI concepts to executives, customers, clinical stakeholders, and commercial teams.
  • A bachelor’s degree in computer science, healthcare management, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred

  • Experience in healthcare technology, especially payer/provider workflows, Risk Adjustment, Quality/HEDIS, medical record retrieval, or clinical data.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA, HITRUST, NCQA, and CMS requirements as they apply to AI-enabled products.
  • Experience building AI evaluation or benchmarking programs, or publishing AI performance results externally.
  • A master’s degree or MBA.

How Success Is Measured

  • Business impact. Measurable revenue, retention, operational savings, or productivity attributable to AI products.
  • AI product adoption. How much customers and end users actually use released AI capabilities.
  • Model and product performance. Accuracy, precision, confidence, workflow effectiveness, and capability-specific KPIs. For example, Smart Overread targets 2 to 3x the random error-detection rate on prioritized charts while keeping random sampling for objective customer accuracy reporting.
  • Speed to value. How quickly a validated opportunity reaches production, including prototype-to-decision cycle time.
  • Portfolio execution. Delivery against the agreed AI roadmap and priorities.
  • Responsible deployment. Every AI release meets customer, contractual, compliance, security, and governance requirements.

Overview

Why NexGen?

NexGen Contracting, the self-perform arm of Gray, is based in Franklin, TN, and specializes in executing turnkey project scopes, including concrete, steel, millwright, and finishes. Why Gray?

Gray is a fully integrated, global service provider deeply rooted in engineering, design, and construction, along with smart manufacturing and equipment manufacturing services. Consistently ranked as a leader in the industry, we focus on the following markets for domestic and international customers: Food & Beverage, Manufacturing, Automotive, Distribution, Mission Critical, and Commercial.

Founded in 1960, Gray’s robust offering enables us to create one-of-a-kind solutions at the highest levels of customization, delivering unmatched precision and partnership to some of the world’s most sophisticated organizations. Still, these areas don’t define Gray—our people do. Passion, commitment, and a great team spirit all speak to the team members at Gray.

Responsibilities

Who we want… (Requirements)

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Construction Management, Paralegal Studies, or a related field; an equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered. Juris Doctor (J.D.) or paralegal certification preferred.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in contractor licensing, regulatory compliance, contract administration, construction law, or risk management; construction industry experience strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of multi-state contractor licensing requirements, including reciprocity, qualifier, continuing education, and financial/experience thresholds.
  • Familiarity with business licensing, Secretary of State filings and entity compliance, and state and local tax requirements that affect construction projects.
  • Experience coordinating vendor and subcontractor pre-qualification, including collecting and organizing financial, safety, insurance, bonding, and licensing documentation.
  • Understanding of construction contracts (prime contracts, subcontracts, and purchase orders), including insurance, indemnity, notice, and flow-down provisions.
  • Strong legal and regulatory research skills, with the ability to interpret statutes, regulations, and agency guidance and turn them into clear, actionable requirements.
  • Exceptional organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage a high volume of deadlines, renewals, and filings across many jurisdictions at once.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable corresponding with state and local agencies, subcontractors, and company leadership.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Monday.com, Trade Tapp, or similar compliance tracking and project management platforms preferred.
  • Background in construction litigation, arbitration, or claims support is a plus.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and handle confidential information with discretion.

The new team member should be an energetic, self-motivated individual who enjoys a team environment, as well as a passion for collaboration and professional development. If you are a high achiever striving to exceed expectations in a fast-paced innovative company, then Gray is the place for you.

The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Qualifications

What we expect… (Essential Functions)

The Loss Prevention and Compliance Coordinator protects NexGen from avoidable regulatory, licensing, and compliance-related losses. This role is NexGen’s single point of accountable ownership for contractor and business licensing, entity compliance, tax research, and subcontractor compliance across all projects nationwide. It also coordinates vendor pre-qualification between NexGen, the decision makers, and project teams, and supports Operations with contract management. It brings work previously handled by an outside licensing vendor fully in-house.

Contractor Licensing

  • Lead and manage all contractor licensing (statewide, county/local, and specialty) for NexGen projects nationwide.
  • Review new project pursuits to confirm jurisdiction (state, county, and city) and scope of work and determine the contractor licenses required before work begins.
  • Research contractor licensing requirements and manage the licensing process from initial project review through approval, including application preparation, supporting documentation, agency correspondence, deficiency resolution, and ongoing compliance requirements.
  • Manage annual license renewals, qualifier continuing education tracking, and specialized contractor license research and applications so that no lapse affects project execution or reciprocity in other states.

Business Licensing & Entity Compliance

  • Research, obtain, and maintain required business licenses and registrations in jurisdictions where NexGen operates.
  • Prepare and coordinate Secretary of State filings, annual reports, and related compliance activities to maintain good standing, working closely with accounting on fees, payments, and supporting documentation.

State & Local Tax Research

  • Research state and local tax, registration, and other jurisdictional requirements for project locations nationwide.
  • Partner with Accounting, Project Controls, and Job Cost teams to support accurate project setup and cost allocation.

Vendor Pre-Qualification & Subcontractor Compliance

  • Coordinate vendor and subcontractor pre-qualification activities, including collecting, organizing, and submitting required financial, safety, insurance, bonding, licensing, and reference information.
  • Track pre-qualification status and communicate updates to decision makers and project teams to support procurement and mobilization schedules.
  • Maintain subcontractor compliance records in TradeTapp, including licensing, insurance, and renewal tracking.

Contract Management Support

  • Support Operations in reviewing and administering contracts, subcontracts, and purchase orders for licensing, insurance, indemnity, notice, and other compliance-related requirements, escalating significant risks as appropriate.
  • Assist with contract preparation, routing, tracking, and record maintenance, including key dates, obligations, and deliverables.
  • Support Change Management activities by maintaining contract documentation related to notices, change orders, claims, and disputes.

Tracking, Reporting & Risk Documentation

  • Maintain licensing and compliance tracking systems, records, and reporting tools to provide visibility into licensing status, renewals, and compliance obligations.
  • Keep compliance documentation organized and audit-ready, ensuring records are complete and defensible.
  • Identify potential compliance risks, communicate gaps, and recommend corrective actions to leadership and project teams.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this position, the team member is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, use hands, reach with hands or arms and talk or hear. Generally, normal office environment where noise level is moderate and temperature/humidity is controlled. Overtime may be required.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

  • Experience leading a Secure Development Lifecycle and application security testing program (SAST, SCA, secret scanning, DAST, fuzzing) in engineering teams.
  • Practical experience assessing the security of AI and LLM features and agentic AI systems, such as prompt injection, data leakage, model supply chain risk, tool and MCP server permissions, and agent sandboxing.
  • Experience using AI to automate security work, such as AI-assisted code review, triage or threat modeling.
  • Track record of building developer security training and tools that engineering teams adopt, including guidance on secure coding with AI assistants.

💡 Preferred Qualifications

jobs.description:
Why Patients Need You


Field & Patient Access is an evolving and highly important area for the success of Primary Care. Due to the complexity of the patient journey in many Primary Care therapeutic areas, up to 60% of primary care medications never get dispensed after an HCP writes the prescription. The role of Primary Care Access and Reimbursement is to remove barriers to access through education and streamlined processes that accelerate fulfillment, helping appropriate patients get access to the medication their HCP has prescribed.


What You Will Achieve


The Field Access & Reimbursement Strategy and Enablement Director will work across a broad, multi-disciplinary group of internal and external stakeholders to develop, evolve, and lead projects & programs to advance the Field Access and Reimbursement group’s mission to accelerate fulfillment for appropriate patients. They will develop a process of continuous improvement measured by clearly defined key performance indicators that serve as benchmarks for success across the platform. The Field Access & Reimbursement Strategy and Enablement Director brings organizational excellence, project management expertise, and analytical rigor together with a deep understanding of Access and Reimbursement priorities and operations — driving seamless execution of operating plans and supporting their continuous evolution.

This role advances Field Access and Reimbursement by continuously improving key operational areas: infrastructure, engagement frameworks, project management, documentation, training, the operating model, analytics and reporting, digital and information platforms, third-party license agreements, resourcing, meeting planning, and budget management — the latter in partnership with the Field and Patient Access Strategy and Enablement Team Lead. The Field Access & Reimbursement Strategy and Enablement Director reports to the Field and Patient Access Strategy and Enablement Team Lead.

How You Will Achieve It

  • Work with Cross-functional Partners, Field Access and Reimbursement Leadership, Marketing/Commercial Leads, Medical Leadership, Legal, Compliance, Patient Services and others to identify key themes and lead initiatives/projects needed to advance productivity, efficiency, and results.
  • Current support includes but is not limited to the Migraine portfolio, Vaccines portfolio, and future Primary Care launches (i.e. obesity)
  • Identify and prioritize the right continuous improvement projects, processes, and resources, working with key stakeholders to advance productivity and support the strategy and execution of quarterly Latest Estimate forecast submissions and the annual Strategic & Operating Plans and budgets.
  • Lead efforts to evolve Field Access and Reimbursement workflows and SOPs as needed, aligned to current guardrails and approved ways of working.
  • Partner cross-functionally to improve training, build capability plans, and help roll out those plans for Field Access and Reimbursement teams and Regional Directors.
  • Partner cross-functionally with key colleagues across functional areas (Patient Services, and others) to evolve, maintain, improve, and enhance Field Access and Reimbursement digital platforms and capabilities, ensuring ongoing alignment, consistency, and efficiency.
  • Partner cross-functionally with internal teams and, as needed, external stakeholders to deliver insights and execute initiatives that evolve the Field Access and Reimbursement approach and drive results.
  • Lead recurring readouts to leadership on Field Access and Reimbursement execution, combining quantitative metrics and qualitative insights as part of Control Tower reporting. Cadence defined by leadership or as needed.
  • Analyze data and generate insights to inform strategic decisions at all levels of Primary Care Access & Reimbursement from the territory level to executive directives.
  • Lead Field Access and Reimbursement in the following: managing territory alignments and updates, enhancing and managing training needs, quarterly business reviews, compliance updates, tracking, supporting strategic planning and pull through for National, Regional, and Fast Start meetings.
  • Work with Field Access and Reimbursement Leadership, Legal, Compliance, and other key stakeholders to evolve the role, responsibilities, and remit of the team to better support patients
  • Serve as primary point of contact with vendors, where appropriate, in collaboration with the Field and Patient Access Strategy and Enablement Team Lead, supporting contracting, procurement, and delivery of key projects.
  • In partnership with the Enablement team lead, contribute to or lead, where appropriate, DSU and PI reporting and overall program requirements.
  • Work across Field & Patient Access Enablement, CMO, and other customer-facing teams to accelerate ways of working programs and key initiatives.
  • Partner with Field Strategy and Enablement Director and Strategy and Innovation Enablement Director to continuously improve ways of working across Field Access and Reimbursement and Patient Engagement, ensuring alignment with compliance requirements and approved guardrails.
  • Pull through AI strategy in partnership with the Field and Patient Access Strategy and Enablement Team Lead and other cross-functional partners, helping build, stand up, and drive adoption of the strategy across the team.
  • Contribute to key operational projects and initiatives across the broader Primary Care Field & Patient Access function.

Qualifications

  • Must-Have
  • 8+ years of pharmaceutical, biotech, or medical marketing/sales with extensive external healthcare market and advanced customer / health system knowledge.
  • Previous experience in Access and Reimbursement, leadership, or operations/enablement, with a demonstrated track record of high performance or specialized technical skills gained through cross-functional leadership roles.
  • Experience leading others in a matrix organization with the ability to manage without direct authority.
  • Ability to influence key stakeholders internally and externally with proven executive communication skills and leadership qualities.
  • Forward looking and results oriented with effective planning, prioritization, and organizational project skills.
  • Strong and proven project management skills demonstrating the ability to deliver multiple time horizon focused projects simultaneously in the short-term and long-term.
  • Track record of leading and managing complex programs to deliver improved outcomes.
  • Strong strategic skills including effectiveness in identifying and addressing major strategic challenges (e.g., shifting market environment) and the ability to balance short-term needs with long-term vision.
  • Strong interpersonal skills are required, as well as excellent written, verbal communication, and presentation skills to address Leadership and external audiences.
  • Proven experience in working with a compliance first mindset.
  • Good judgement and high ethics are a must.

· Headquarters knowledge and experience, with proven experience working across cross-functional HQ departments, teams, and business units.

Job Title: Biostatistics Sr Mgr

Job Location: Washington D.C., District of Columbia, United States

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.


Biostatistics Sr Manager


What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will achieve results through detailed goal setting, accountability measures, effective partnership, performance management, collaboration with other groups and a dedication to serving customers, both inside and outside of, Global Study Operations (GSO).


The Senior Biostatistics Manager independently leads sophisticated studies and projects in the oncology therapeutic area, ensuring that the statistical aspects of clinical activities meet required standards and are robust and valid. Will also influence and supply to strategy development, defend statistical approaches and represent GBS through participating in and collaborating with multidisciplinary project teams. Specific duties include:

  • Utilizing knowledge and expertise to inform and provide sound statistical guidance to areas and teams in clinical development, reimbursement, and medical affairs.
  • Implementing, managing and supporting standards, technical quality and consistent approaches in strategy, study design and statistical analysis.
  • Planning and executing statistical contributions to protocols, Flash Memos and Clinical Study Reports (CSRs).
  • Providing input for clinical publications and regulatory filing documents.
  • Leading all aspects of work performed by study statisticians.
  • Performing statistical and exploratory analysis of studies/projects and developing conclusions and recommendations.
  • Anticipating and communicating resource and quality challenges that could impact results or timelines.
  • Solid understanding of regulatory guidelines in oncology drug development.
  • Staying current in developments in the field of statistics in drug development (innovative trial design) and Amgen’s statistical policies, procedures and strategies.
  • Contributing to process improvements and operational efficiencies.

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will use our unique contributions to serve patients. The Biostatistical professional we seek is an emerging leader with these qualifications.

Basic Qualifications


Doctorate degree

Or

Master’s degree and 4 years of Biostatistics experience

Or

Bachelor’s degree and 6 years of Biostatistics experience


Preferred Qualifications

  • Doctorate degree in biostatics or statistics.
  • 5 or more years of pharma/biotech statistical experience.
  • Life cycle drug development experience (pre-clinical, clinical and post-marketing).
  • Experience with oncology drug development.
  • Proven in leadership and motivating multi-functional team to advance complex projects to completion and thoughtfully negotiate and influence
  • Strong verbal and written communication combined with organizational skills and cross-cultural sensitivity
  • Statistical leadership and contribution to regulatory and reimbursement submissions.
  • Strong working knowledge of theoretical and applied statistics and of regulatory guidelines.
  • Experience working effectively in a globally dispersed team environment with cross-cultural partners.

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include:

  • A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts

  • Stock-based long-term incentives

The Business Development Consultant owns the recruiting lifecycle for assigned prospective financial advisors, from pipeline development and discovery through affiliation, contracting, and transition to onboarding. The role builds consultative relationships with small to mid-sized opportunities, communicates Cetera’s value proposition, evaluates advisor fit, and advances qualified prospects through disciplined deal execution. The position partners with business development, legal, finance, compliance, onboarding, transition, and operations teams to deliver a coordinated advisor experience. Success is measured by quality pipeline development, recruiting goal attainment, timely deal progression, accurate documentation, and effective transition handoffs.

Candidates must be located on the west coast.

Key Duties & Responsibilities

  • Own and execute the end-to-end recruiting process for an assigned territory or advisor segment, from initial outreach through contracting and transition to onboarding.

  • Develop and manage a consistent pipeline of prospective financial advisors through outbound calling, email, social media, networking, referrals, and targeted campaigns.

  • Build consultative relationships with small to mid-sized advisor opportunities and communicate Cetera’s platform, services, technology, affiliation options, and transition support.

  • Assess advisor fit by reviewing practice profile, book-of-business information, growth potential, business needs, financial information, due diligence materials, and alignment with Cetera’s model.

  • Deliver business presentations and lead discovery, diligence, offer, and negotiation discussions for smaller or less complex opportunities, escalating larger or higher-risk matters to senior leaders.

  • Coordinate proposals, transition assistance packages, contracting documents, home-office visits, meetings, and final diligence sessions to support timely and accurate deal execution.

  • Partner with legal, finance, compliance, onboarding, transition, operations, and business development stakeholders to resolve issues and create a seamless prospect-to-onboarding handoff.

  • Maintain complete candidate profiles, activity records, financial information, due diligence materials, pipeline stages, and forecasts in Salesforce, Microsoft Excel, and related reporting tools.

  • Analyze advisor business metrics and recruiting activity to support deal positioning, prioritization, pipeline reporting, and recommendations on next steps.

  • Develop and use sales enablement materials and share process improvement recommendations that strengthen recruiting effectiveness and the prospective advisor experience.

Experience & Qualifications

Required Education:

  • Bachelor's Degree Business, Finance, Marketing, Communications, or a related field.

Required Experience:

  • FINRA Series 7 and Series 65 (or 66) or to obtain within 6 months of start date.

  • 5-7 years experience in financial services, advisor recruiting, business development, relationship management, consultative sales, or a related field

  • Experience managing a recruiting or sales pipeline and advancing opportunities through close.

OR equivalent combination of experience and education in lieu of above.

Other Requirements

  • This role is 100% remote

  • 30-40% travel

    • Ability to travel by plane and car regularly for in person prospect and home office meetings

  • Knowledge of financial advisor business models, broker-dealer or RIA affiliation, and advisor transition considerations.

  • Proficiency with Salesforce or a similar CRM and Microsoft Excel for pipeline management, activity tracking, and reporting.

  • Ability to deliver business presentations, conduct consultative discovery, evaluate advisor fit, and coordinate multiple stakeholders and deadlines.

Compensation:

The salary range for this role is $90,000, plus competitive incentive compensation package. Compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years and depth of experience, certifications, and location. Compensation ranges may differ significantly due to geography and cost of labor considerations.

Position Title: Executive Assistant

Position Location: United States, Remote

Salary

QC Servion recognizes salary ranges from job boards do not necessarily reflect our pay ranges. In many instances we out-compete those ranges for well-qualified candidates.

Why This Role, Why Now

To keep pace with scaling our Ecosystem of companies, we are seeking high-level Executive Assistants to partner directly with C-Suite executives. This is not a general administrative role. It is for seasoned Executive Assistants who have operated at the very top of an organization, who treat calendar, travel, expense and inbox management as a craft and who use AI every day to work faster, sharper and smarter.

If you are the person executives trust to run their day, protect their time and anticipate what they need before they ask, we want to talk with you.

Job Summary

The Executive Assistant is a trusted, high-touch partner to C-Suite executives across our Ecosystem of companies, ensuring seamless execution of strategic initiatives in a fully remote, fast-moving, high-growth environment. Drawing on deep organizational savvy, executive presence, advanced technical and AI acumen and a polished, service-oriented mindset, this professional shields senior leaders from operational friction so they can stay focused on the decisions that move the business.

The Executive Administrative Assistant will be self-directed on day-to-day work, receive high-level direction on new projects and assignments and execute work of complex scope with minimal oversight. This individual will communicate and operate in line with organizational goals and values, exercise sound judgment and absolute discretion, and adapt quickly as priorities, tools and the organization itself evolve.

Essential Functions

Executive Calendar & Inbox Management (40%)

  • Own complex, multi-time-zone calendars for one or more C-Suite executives; anticipate conflicts, focus time and proactively negotiate solutions with other executive offices
  • Triage high-volume executive inboxes: prioritize, flag, respond on the executive’s behalf, where authorized, and surface only what requires their attention
  • Draft, proofread and format executive correspondence, briefing materials, slide decks and proposals to a polished, executive-ready standard
  • Prepare executives for every meeting with agendas, pre-reads, background and follow-up actions
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders, including partners and senior leaders

Travel & Expense Management (25%)

  • Plan and manage domestic and international executive travel end-to-end, including complex multi-leg itineraries, visas, risk-mitigation protocols, ground transportation and on-site logistics
  • Rebook and resolve travel disruptions in real time, with contingency plans ready before they are needed
  • Prepare, reconcile and submit expense reports accurately and on time; track receipts, maintain budget and policy compliance, and partner with Finance on corrections and audits

Executive Meeting & Event Support (15%)

  • Assist in executive and leadership and committee meetings, including scheduling, materials assembly, distribution and secure document handling
  • Assist in coordinating hybrid and virtual leadership off-sites, annual strategy sessions and executive briefings end-to-end
  • Capture and track decisions and action items; ensure timely follow-through

Leadership Reporting & Cross-Functional Coordination (10%)

  • Assemble and circulate leadership status reports, synthesizing inputs from multiple companies and departments into concise executive summaries
  • Track action items and follow-ups across functional teams, ensuring timely completion and transparent communication
  • Provide project-management / coordination support for strategic initiatives as needed

AI Enablement, Information Governance & Process Optimization (10%)

  • Use AI tools (Microsoft Copilot, Claude) daily to draft, summarize, research, prepare briefings and automate repetitive work
  • Identify and implement process improvements, automations and AI-enabled workflows that scale executive support as the Ecosystem grows
  • Maintain confidential files and records, ensuring adherence to policies and security protocols, including safe and appropriate use of AI with sensitive information

Completion of Assigned Tasks and Deliverables on Time and on Budget

  • Performs Other Related Duties as Assigned

Required Core Skills: Impeccable Execution Expected

Candidates must demonstrate mastery in each of the following. These are assessed directly during the interview process.

  • Calendaring: Proven ownership of complex, multi-executive, multi-time-zone calendars at the C-Suite level, with zero tolerance for errors
  • Travel: Complex domestic and international travel planning and real-time issue resolution for senior executives
  • Expense Management: Accurate, timely expense reporting and reconciliation using enterprise systems
  • Email Triage: Proven ability to manage high-volume executive inboxes, prioritize with sound judgment and communicate on the executive’s behalf
  • AI Use & Adaptability: Strong, hands-on daily use of AI tools for drafting, summarizing, research and automation, plus the adaptability to learn new tools and workflows quickly as the organization scales

Position Requirements

Advanced level for all the following unless otherwise noted:

  • Executive presence and the ability to interact confidently and credibly with C-Suite executives and external partners
  • Absolute discretion with highly confidential information, including transactions, personnel and financial data
  • Advanced skill in Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, SharePoint)
  • Advanced skill in using artificial intelligence and generative AI tools, with a strong emphasis on AI-assisted research, drafting and workflow automation
  • Knowledge of administrative procedures and systems, including managing files and records, designing forms and document control
  • Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy in all deliverables
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, technical and non-technical
  • Ability to anticipate needs, think several steps ahead and act without being asked
  • Ability to work iteratively: clarifying scope, giving interim updates, following up proactively and confirming completion
  • Ability to thrive in a high-growth, rapidly changing environment, adapting quickly to new priorities, people, companies and tools
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet close deadlines while managing multiple priorities simultaneously
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively with remote team members
  • Ability to work successfully in a remote environment through strong communication, self-motivation, proactiveness and resourcefulness in a distraction-free workspace

Qualifications

  • Experience supporting a CEO, C-Suite or Board of Directors
  • Experience supporting multiple executives or companies simultaneously within a portfolio, holding company or high growth organization
  • Demonstrated examples of AI-enabled process improvements you have personally implemented

Physical Demands

The following physical demands must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of

this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential

functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is:

  • Travel is defined as physically leaving home on behalf of business activities including but not limited to client sites, meetings with other employees, meetings for business development purposes, running errands on behalf of the business, attending industry conferences, etc.

jobs.excerpt: A Note On How To Reach Us We're truly grateful that so many people have Foundant on their radar — it means a lot that our work resonates with others.
jobs.description:
A Note On How To Reach Us

We're truly grateful that so many people have Foundant on their radar — it means a lot that our work resonates with others. That said, due to the high volume of direct messages and emails we receive, cold outreach isn't the preferred way to be considered for a role, and we're not able to prioritize applications submitted this way. To apply for open positions, please visit our careers page, which is the fastest and most effective route to being considered.

About Foundant

At Foundant, we build mission-critical software for the social good ecosystem — helping foundations, grantmakers, nonprofits, and community organizations streamline their work, strengthen relationships, and maximize their impact. We serve the giving community worldwide with a comprehensive suite of solutions spanning grant management, community foundation software, and giving analytics.

We're a unified company shaped by strong roots across our product portfolio, and we operate with intention and purpose. Our team of ~350 people across six countries is connected by a shared North Star: to be the trusted partner and strategic advisor to the communities we serve.

Where You’ll Work:
  • As a remote-first workplace, we believe in offering flexibility and the freedom to work where it suits you best, while staying connected through technology. Our global network of talent is supported by physical office hubs and virtual collaboration, fostering a dynamic environment where innovation and growth thrive.
  • With office locations in Bozeman, MT, Toronto, Canada, and Dublin, Ireland, you'll be part of a globally connected team. Whether you're working remotely or from one of our office locations, you'll be contributing to a vibrant, collaborative culture focused on driving meaningful impact across the world.
WhatYou’llDo:
  • You’ll build your own pipeline. Consistent, personalized outreach to government agencies that administer grant programs is the foundation of your results. You see it as the best way to sharpen your craft, because earning a response to a cold email or call is the hardest part of selling. Marketing and BDR-sourced leads are a welcome bonus on top of your own efforts, never a substitute for them.
  • You’ll own the full sales cycle and its results, carrying each opportunity from first conversation through a signed deal.
  • You’ll run discovery that goes past the surface request, listening for the mission, constraints, and outcomes each organization is working toward, reading both the people and the process, and shaping solutions that fit what they’re trying to achieve.
  • You’ll deliver clear, compelling demos and proposals that connect Foundant’s grant management solutions, including our purpose-built AI, to the results your prospect cares about.
  • You’ll drive government decision-making instead of waiting on it. Public-sector buying cycles can move slowly, so you’ll map the decision process early, line up sponsors and clear next steps, and create a genuine sense of urgency tied to what matters to your buyer, such as budget cycles, grant deadlines, and program timelines.
  • You’ll work through multi-stakeholder buying processes, including public-sector procurement requirements, committee reviews, and security reviews, keeping every stakeholder informed and bringing in your director and senior colleagues as deals grow more complex.
  • You’ll bring your government experience to help us grow the segment, spotting new agencies, programs, and use cases to pursue and sharing what you’re hearing from buyers with your director and cross-functional partners.
  • You’ll think critically about how to position Foundant for each buyer and learn how our internal teams work together, so you know who to involve, when, and why.
  • You’ll use AI to work smarter, from account research to outreach to proposal preparation, and you’ll apply critical thinking to how you use it: checking its outputs, protecting data, and keeping your own judgment in the lead.
  • You’ll partner with Marketing, Revenue Operations, Product, and Client teams, and hand off every new client with full context so the team that takes over is set up to succeed from day one.
  • You’ll learn from senior Account Executives and your director, asking for feedback on discovery, demos, and deal strategy and applying it in your next conversation.
  • You’ll hold yourself accountable for accurate pipeline data and forecasts in our CRM, using that data to prioritize your time and flag risks early, including your own.
  • Other duties as assigned.
WhatYou’llNeed:
  • 2–5 years of B2B SaaS sales experience
  • Demonstrated history of meeting or exceeding sales targets in a full-cycle sales role
  • Experience building your own pipeline through proactive, personalized outbound outreach
  • Experience navigating public-sector buying processes, including procurement, committee, or security reviews, and moving them forward with urgency
  • Sound judgment and critical thinking, including the ability to use AI tools thoughtfully and evaluate their output
  • Proficiency with a CRM platform for pipeline management and forecasting
  • Required: Government grantmaking experience in the social good space
  • Must be legally eligible to work in the United States
  • A plus: Broader public sector experience
WhatYou’llBring to our Team Dynamics:

Adaptive Achievement

Owns a pipeline and a number, building that pipeline through self-driven outreach and driving deals through shifting buyer priorities and slow, multi-stakeholder buying cycles by creating urgency rather than waiting on decisions. Follows through when a deal gets hard, not just when it’s going well, and takes responsibility for outcomes, including misses.

Productive Collaboration

Works hand in hand with Marketing, Revenue Operations, Product, and Client teams, applying emotional intelligence to build trust across the organization. Hands off new clients with context, so the relationship doesn’t restart at signature.

Service Orientation

Treats every prospect conversation as the start of a long-term relationship: listens for the mission behind the request, reads what’s said and unsaid, and recommends what will genuinely serve the client’s outcomes, even when it isn’t the fastest path to a close.

Business Insight

Understands how government agencies fund, administer, and report on their grant programs, and connects Foundant’s solutions to those outcomes. Thinks critically about positioning and about how AI is used in their own work, and uses pipeline data to prioritize accounts and forecast accurately.

Active Learning

Ramps quickly on Foundant’s solutions and the segment’s funding landscape, stays curious about how government funding and procurement are evolving, asks for feedback from clients, peers, and deal reviews, applies it noticeably in the next conversation, and adjusts without being told.

Why You’ll Love Working at Foundant:
  • At the heart of everything we do is a commitment to innovation and making a positive impact. Whether you’re working on projects that empower not-for-profits, community foundations, or corporations, your contributions will help drive real-world change.
  • We offer competitive salary and benefits, including tuition, and lifestyle reimbursements, and bespoke mindfulness and fitness initiatives.
  • With our Flexible PTO policy, you’ll have the freedom to manage your time in a way that supports your personal well-being and professional success.
  • We’re committed to your professional and personal development. With our merger, you'll have the chance to collaborate across teams, giving you exposure to diverse ideas, expertise, and projects that span multiple industries.
  • As part of a larger organization, you’ll have even more opportunities to grow your career. Whether it’s exploring new roles, leadership opportunities, or shifting to a different department, we support internal mobility to help you achieve your career goals
  • You’ll enjoy autonomy and responsibility, empowering you to approach your work creatively and independently, fostering innovation and independent thought.
  • Employee recognition is a core part of our culture. When you do a great job, we make sure everyone knows about it!

Foundant is an equal opportunity employer, committed to building a diverse workforce that represents the communities we serve. We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified candidates, and will consider all applicants without regard to race, color, citizenship, religion, sex, marital/family status, sexual orientation, gender identity, Indigenous status, age, disability, or individuals who may require accommodation.

Foundant is also committed to providing accommodations throughout the interview and employment process. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates participating in all aspects of the selection process. Velera is the nation’s premier payments credit union service organization (CUSO) and an integrated fintech solutions provider. The company serves more than 4,000 financial institutions throughout North America, operating with velocity to help our clients keep pace with the rapid momentum of change and fuel growth in the new era of financial services. Our purpose: We accelerate partners’ success through innovative financial technology solutions and inspired service.

The Opportunity:

The Risk Prevention Analyst is responsible for providing operational risk assessments leveraging fraud mitigation tools, focusing on analysis, design, and artificial intelligence (AI) technology associated with fraud mitigation strategies, call queue creation, monitoring, support, and management using quantitative methods to review data and increase efficiency, productivity, effectiveness and savings. Seeking a skilled Risk Analyst who will provide support for external clients and internal staff on fraud detection and prevention matters, inquiries, and solutions to meet client and business needs. Additionally, the role involves writing rules and creating custom solutions for clients, monitoring fraud for their client group, identifying risk exposure based on fraud trends and data, and determining mitigation measures. This role involves direct interaction with senior-level management at the financial institution and within Velera, as well as regular coordination with the Fraud Detection Work Center (FDWC), Velera Service Centers, multiple internal departments, and 3rd party vendor personnel.

Day in the Life:

  • Develop and implement Fraud strategies leveraging transaction data (credit/debit cards), machine learning models and advanced analytics tools to mitigate fraud losses and maintain superior customer experience.

  • Manage and optimize existing strategies effectively controlling risks due to first party and third-party fraud. Design, tests and understand the risk and customer experience trade-offs.

  • Coordinate the Risk Analytics team's tasks and ensure adherence to established turnaround times and SLAs; manage projects assigned to the team; Ensure quality of all team outputs.

  • Maintain awareness of member client fraud trends and suggest internal procedure changes to Risk Analytics Manager to remain efficient.

  • Ensure risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.

  • Responsible for reporting risks identified to the appropriate team and/or management.

  • Additionally, responsible for managing, monitoring and reporting risks within your work area's scope, including, but not limited to Information Security risks.

  • Regular and reliable attendance is required. Some on-call work is required.

  • This position may require early/late hours and availability during weekends to ensure client support on fraud monitoring or mitigation.

  • Bring innovative/out of the box thinking to solve problems and make recommendations.

  • Functional knowledge of common fraud patterns with endless curiosity to seek out anomalies and get to the core of a problem.

  • The ability to prioritize and make quick decisions under tight deadlines

  • Remain current with industry and client fraud trends.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering or Economics or related field or combination of education and experience required.

  • Five (5) years within the financial service industry required.

  • Three (3) years professional experience in risk analytics, mitigating risk and/or fraud services required.

  • Payments processing system knowledge preferred.

  • Experience with, , Fraud Detection Work Center and/or FDR system experience required.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Deep experience working with fraud detection strategies, rules tuning, and fraud modeling.

  • Strong proficiency with SQL; Ability to analyze large, complex datasets and derive actionable insights.

  • Experience with fraud orchestration and decisioning tools (e.g., DefenseEdge, Falcon, Advance Defense, Fraud Navigator) preferred.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Join ICOMAT – Revolutionising the Future of Lightweight Manufacturing!
jobs.description:
Join ICOMAT – Revolutionising the Future of Lightweight Manufacturing!

iCOMAT is an advanced manufacturing company that invented Rapid Tow Shearing (RTS) - the only proven technology for producing defect-free curved-fiber composite parts at industrial scale. We deliver the lightest structures possible for aerospace, automotive, defense, and space, at a rate and cost efficiency that far exceeds existing composite production processes.

We build and operate automated factories for composite materials, delivering components to Tier 1 suppliers and OEMs. The business has three main divisions: development of automated production machines, development of software design and production tools, and operation of the factory. We work with 25+ customers and completed the largest ever Series A in composites manufacturing to fuel a significant scale-up, with growth plans that will see the business multiply in size over the next two to three years and expand operations into the UK, Europe and the US.

The business has currently more than 130,000 sqm of production capacity with manufacturing facilities in the UK (Gloucester and Swindon) and the US (Dayton, Ohio); a Hardware R&D Centre in Bristol, UK; and a Software R&D Centre in Athens, Greece.

We are hiring Senior Software Engineers to join our in-house Software Engineering team and build iCOMAT’s manufacturing and business operations system. This platform is iCOMAT’s central hub for executing R&D and manufacturing activities, connecting ERP, production scheduling, machine telemetry, shop-floor execution and business operations across our manufacturing sites.

What will you be doing?

From day one, you will be building and shipping systems that are used daily by planners, manufacturing engineers, and R&D teams to run real factories.

The software platform is built on a modern web-stack and runs entirely using on-prem infrastructure, with cloud adoption ramping up in 2027. All aspects of iCOMAT’s business and manufacturing activities are within scope, from ERP and SaaS integrations to real-time telemetry streams from the machines on our production floor. The goal is to provide a real-time view of our factories that enables autonomous decision making to deliver high quality, repeatable composite manufacturing at scale.

Depending on your strengths, your focus will sit across one or more of the platform's three pillars:

  1. Web application development. Building production-grade, full-stack features in Nuxt, TypeScript and Postgres, including asynchronous and event-driven workloads (queues, Pub/Sub) and real-time interfaces over websockets.

  2. Data orchestration. Designing and operating data pipelines and warehousing (BigQuery or similar) with orchestration frameworks such as Dagster, Airflow or Prefect, in Python.

  3. Agent Development and Orchestration. Deploying autonomous agents that integrate with ICOMAT’s business systems and operating context to power AI-enabled decision making across the business.

As well as writing software code, you will be expected to contribute across much of the software development lifecycle, from co-designing requirements with end users on the factory floor, to validating MVPs, and executing the build, test and release of production-standard software.

What does success look like?

As a manufacturing business, our success is defined by the quality of the parts we produce, the repeatability of our manufacturing processes, and the reliability of the operations behind them.

iCOMAT’s business and manufacturing platform builds on this by giving our teams a single, trusted view of the factory — replacing fragile spreadsheets and disconnected tools with software that makes scheduling, execution, and reporting faster, clearer, and dependable.

From a personal perspective, we value engineers who can turn ambiguous operational problems into robust software systems, communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and deliver production-quality tools that are trusted by the business.

iCOMAT is setting the standard for how advanced composite structures are designed, manufactured, and industrialised at scale. Your contributions will build the operational backbone for world-leading technology that will be embedded in the next generation of aerospace and defence hardware.

How do you fit in?

You will be joining iCOMAT's in-house software engineering team, reporting directly to the Head of AI and working alongside other Senior Software Engineers. This is a small, senior team developing the software foundations for iCOMAT's design, manufacturing, and operations capability.

The current team brings experience across manufacturing and engineering, machine learning and production-grade software delivery. We work closely with iCOMAT's planning, manufacturing engineering, and production teams to understand the problems that matter most, then turn those problems into reliable internal products.

This role would suit someone who enjoys contributing to a team where the boundaries between product thinking, engineering judgement, and software delivery are deliberately close.

For this role, your contribution will be to deepen the team's capability across full-stack web development, data engineering, and cloud/platform operations — and to help set the engineering standards for a platform that the whole business will come to depend on. You will bring practical software engineering discipline, curiosity about manufacturing operations, and the confidence to collaborate with domain experts to build software that is robust, maintainable, and genuinely useful.

Who you are?

Innovative. You are comfortable developing novel solutions for truly complex problems.

Independent.You don't shy away from open-ended problems and enjoy helping shape end-to-end solutions. You are comfortable working as an individual contributor as part of a multi-functional team.

Product-minded. Software is more than just code. You embrace the opportunity to contribute across the end-to-end software development lifecycle and care about delivering a solution that creates real, measurable value for the business.

Operations-led. You enjoy working close to the realities of a live production environment — scheduling constraints, machine data, shop-floor workflows — and you are motivated by building software that helps a factory run better every day.

What should you expect?

iCOMAT is on a mission to revolutionise the way engineers design and manufacture with composite materials. We have a build-first methodology and take pride in developing in-house capabilities that cater for our specific needs. Our technology is world-leading, and our software must be capable of supporting demanding operational workflows from the planning office through to the production floor.

You should expect to work on problems where software, data, manufacturing, and product thinking meet. This role will suit someone who enjoys writing high-quality code but also wants to understand how that code changes the way a real factory operates.

iCOMAT is fast paced. The atmosphere is demanding but rewarding. We are operating at the cutting edge of composite manufacturing technology, and we are looking for people who want to help build the operational software foundations that allow that technology to scale.

Our Stack

  • Full Stack Framework: Nuxt

  • Application Database: Postgres

  • Data Orchestration: Currently evaluating Dagster, Prefect and Airflow

  • AI Tooling: Claude Code

  • Version Control & CI/CD: Self-Hosted GitLab

  • Languages: Typescript, Python (bonus points for Go, C++, C#, Julia)

  • Application Hosting: On-prem, docker-based deployments

  • Cloud: GCP & Azure (GCP preferred for new workflows)

Skills and Experience

Essential

  • 5+ years of demonstrable industry experience building and operating production software systems used by real end users

  • 5+ years hands-on software development experience in TypeScript and/or Python. We also value experience in Go, C# and C++.

  • Deep, hands-on expertise in at least two of the platform's three pillars: full-stack web development (Nuxt/Vue or comparable modern framework, Postgres, async/event-driven patterns, websockets); data orchestration (data warehousing such as BigQuery, plus Dagster, Airflow or Prefect); cloud computing (AWS, Azure or GCP; GCP preferred)

  • Solid working knowledge of relational databases, including schema design, migrations, and query performance (Postgres preferred)

  • Familiarity with modern software development practices, such as test-driven development, automated testing, code review, CI/CD, and containerisation

  • Strong first-degree or Masters/PhD in computer science or a STEM-related subject

  • Eligible to work with UK export-controlled material and willing to undergo security screening if required

Desirable

  • Previous start-up or scale-up experience is highly advantageous – we move very fast

  • Experience working in aerospace & defence, manufacturing or logistics

  • Experience developing software for highly regulated and/or export-controlled environments

  • Experience developing software to comply with common information management and cyber security certifications (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2, etc.)

  • Experience integrating with ERP, MES, or other manufacturing/business systems

  • Experience with industrial data protocols and telemetry (e.g. MQTT, OPC-UA) or other high-volume event streams

  • Working knowledge of C# / .NET – some engineering systems run this stack

  • Experience deploying and operating software in self-hosted / on-prem environments

  • Experience developing accessible and intuitive user experiences across a variety of design tools and front-end frameworks

  • Experience developing agentic tools for use by end-users

  • Comfortable using AI coding tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar developer assistants

  • Experience applying machine learning in production environments (e.g. AI Engineer, MLOps, Data Science)

Our Values: Uncompromising Excellence

  • Discipline over excuses. We commit. We follow through. We hold ourselves and each other to the highest standard, especially when the pressure is on.

  • Push the edge. iCOMAT was built on a refusal to accept that curved fiber could not be manufactured at scale. We innovate where others hesitate.

  • Aligned and accountable. Everyone owns their lane, communicates openly, and delivers without being chased. No silos. No ambiguity.

Why iCOMAT?

  • Competitive Salary & Benefits: We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including private healthcare, pension scheme.

  • Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

  • Career Growth Opportunities: Join us at a pivotal time as we scale up, offering unmatched professional growth opportunities in the rapidly advancing field of composite materials.

  • Innovation-Focused Culture: We pride ourselves on our inclusive, forward-thinking work environment. Recognized by Bloomberg as a "UK Startup to Watch," iCOMAT celebrates diversity and encourages all applicants, regardless of background, to apply.

  • Global Impact: Be a part of our mission to redefine lightweight structures for the automotive, aerospace, and space industries, working with some of the most influential companies worldwide.Ready to be part of something big?

Apply now to learn more and join us on our exciting journey!

Ontwikkeling en ondersteuning

Kwaliteit en testing

Samenwerking en productwerking

Change- en releasemanagement

  • Kwaliteit, risico's en stabiliteit bewaken tijdens wijzigingen in productieomgevingen.

📝 Jouw profiel

Je combineert sterke analytische vaardigheden met een nauwkeurige en zelfstandige werkhouding. Je voelt je verantwoordelijk voor je werk, communiceert helder en draagt actief bij aan de samenwerking binnen het team.

  • Kennis van Angular 2 of hoger.
  • Ervaring met relationele databases, bijvoorbeeld Oracle en SQL.
  • Ervaring met unit testing.
  • Kennis van Agile ontwikkelingsmethodieken.
  • Vertrouwd met procesgestuurde organisaties die werken volgens ITIL-processen.

Analytische en persoonlijke vaardigheden
